Title: Kafka cluster ownership, sizing and the Event Hubs fallback are not decided
Detail: Version 4 has no Kafka row at all, because the design then used an outbox without a broker. Architecture v5 makes Kafka the event broker, gives the topic settings of every service topic (12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt) and names Azure Event Hubs Premium as the fallback, but leaves the owner and the sizing of the cluster open, and the architecture team's first decision is exactly that: whether Recovery's topics sit on the bank Kafka platform ACE already uses. Version 5 states the topic settings and the fallback, and adds no owner beyond the roles Architecture v5 names.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9 notes: 'Kafka: topic per service rwb.<name>.events.v1, 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents binary mode, outbox and inbox, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt; Event Hubs Premium is the fallback.' Architecture v5 slide 39 decision 1: 'Host Recovery's business-event topics on the bank Kafka platform ACE already uses (separate topics and ACLs from PII logging); fallback: Azure Event Hubs Kafka endpoint / Owner: Enterprise Architecture, ACE platform team'. Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 3: no Kafka row.
Proposed fix: Close Architecture v5 decision 1 in Wave 0: name the cluster that hosts the 19 service topics and rwb.decision-record.v1, its capacity and its retention, the team that runs it, the ACL model, and the trigger for the Event Hubs fallback. Record the answer in this document and in the event and messaging design.

Proposed fix: Name the calling service for each of the twelve agents in the Ownership Map (sheet Workflows and activities, one row per agent run) before wave 1, on the rule that the service that owns the stage decision starts the run.

Title: The rule result used on a fallback is named for two agents only
Detail: The fallback rule is uniform in the source: if the agent does not answer within 60 seconds, 'the rule result is used and the fallback is recorded'. The Temporal and Drools design names R-UNI-32 for the route agent and the pricing agent only; it does not name the rule, the package or the version that supplies the result for the other ten agents. Without it a fallback cannot be shown to produce the same decision as the rule path.
Evidence: Source slide 8: 'Fallback / If the agent does not answer within 60 seconds, the rule result is used and the fallback is recorded'. Temporal and Drools design slide 13: 'Agent run with rule fallback for the route agent and pricing agent (R-UNI-32)'; slide 14 table: 'AI agent slow: after 60 s the rule result is used (R-UNI-32)'.
Proposed fix: Add one column to the agent policy row naming the rule package and version that supplies the fallback result for each of the twelve agents, and publish it with the rule registry of P7.

Title: The 60 seconds: the whole run or the model call
Detail: The sources set a 60-second limit and do not say what it covers. Source slide 8 starts the clock at 'if the agent does not answer'; Architecture v5 writes 'AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result', which reads as the whole workflow including the tool reads and the guardrail check; the NFR line reads 'AI agent: 60 s, then rule result'. A tool read of 2 s and a guardrail activity therefore sit inside or outside the same 60 s depending on the reading, which changes the budget the model gets.
Evidence: Source slide 8: 'If the agent does not answer within 60 seconds, the rule result is used'; source slide 11: 'DL11 / Agent response target / 60 seconds, then the rule result is used'. Architecture v5 slide 16: 'TMP AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result'; slide 39: 'AI agent runs / rwb-agent: 60 s, or the rule result is used'.
Proposed fix: Set the 60 s on the whole AgentRunWorkflow: the timer starts when the workflow starts and a run that has not passed its guardrails at 60 s falls back. Publish the split (tool budget, model budget) in the agent policy row.

Title: Three Temporal release positions disagree: 1.28.1 in ADR-011, 1.29.7 in the design stack note, 1.30+ required for Nexus and Worker Versioning
Detail: ADR-011 sets the cluster on 'the pinned release SCB IT approves at build' and its consequence names 1.28.1. Architecture v5 slide 23 requires version 1.30+ for Nexus and Worker Versioning and slide 47 lists the upgrade from 1.28.1 as a Wave 0 risk. The Temporal and Drools design notes a local stack of 1.29.7. ADR-016 states 1.30 or later on the pinned release SCB IT approves at build, and the exact released version to pin is not named in any read source.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 23 'version 1.30+'; slide 47 'Temporal upgrade from 1.28.1'; Temporal and Drools design slide 32 note 'local stack 1.29.7, ADR-011 1.28.1'.
Proposed fix: Pin one Temporal release of 1.30 or later in Wave 0 and record it in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1 and in ADR-016.

Title: Event payload property types, formats and required flags are not specified in any source
Detail: The payload column of Event and Messaging Design v4 gives the field names of each event and nothing else (for example EV-01 CaseCreated: 'caseId, caseNo, productGroup, accounts, businessDate'); it states no JSON type, format, nullability or required flag for any field, and no nested object shape for the composite fields (accounts, terms, fields, result, documents). The Arch v5 event catalogue gives the event name, the producer, the topic and the consumers only, with the note that schemas are versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility. The AsyncAPI 3.0 documents of v5 therefore carry the field names as property names with no type, and the gap is recorded rather than a type invented.
Evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Events rows EV-01 to EV-30, column Payload: field names only. Arch v5 slide 42 notes: 'Schemas are versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility; the AsyncAPI document per service is the contract' and gives no field type. Arch v5 slide 35: JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility. No source in the read list gives an event JSON Schema.
Proposed fix: Publish the JSON Schema of each event payload in the registry and copy it into the AsyncAPI documents, or confirm that field names only are the agreed contract for the first release so that each producer owns its schema types in its CON story.

Title: Activity contract jar coordinates are not specified
Detail: Each service publishes an activity contract jar on its own task queue, but no source states the groupId, artifactId or versioning scheme of those jars.
Evidence: Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 names the L4 activity contracts per service; Architecture v5 says no service imports another's code, only its contract jar; neither gives coordinates.
Proposed fix: State the artefact and the Java package root now, and allocate the coordinates with the repositories in the service template work.

Title: Route-services-through-Temporal rule meets REST cells to rwb-source-data
Detail: Slide 13 states that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never REST, and the same matrix gives REST cells from S1, S7 and S8 to rwb-source-data.
Evidence: Slide 13 note: route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never REST, only rwb-source-data touches ACE's tables. Matrix cells S1 to P1, S7 to P1 and S8 to P1 are R.
Proposed fix: Read the rule as covering the five shared capabilities named in the slide note (decision, document, payment, partner, comms); keep the rwb-source-data reference reads as REST, one hop and cached.

Title: The 15 event types named only in the Architecture v5 service catalogue have no payload
Detail: Fifteen event types are named on the service catalogue slides of Architecture v5 and have no row in the v4 event table, so no payload is stated for them: ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished, FileDelivered, FileFailed, RouteDecided, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled, LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, AssetSold, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged. The payload of these types cannot be given without inventing fields.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 service catalogue lines, for example 'EVT rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce', 'EVT rwb.reporting.events.v1: ReportPublished', 'EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult'. Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Events holds EV-01 to EV-30 only.
Proposed fix: Fix the payload of each of the 15 event types in the CON story of the owning service, with IDs and codes only and no personal data, and register the schema before the first consumer is built.

Title: The Ownership Map v1 has no table for rwb-valuation although Architecture v5 names valuations, the D6 route decision and the route agent output
Detail: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives S1 rwb-valuation the resources 'valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output'. The Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet holds no row owned by S1, and the Physical Schema v6 creates no valuation table; only valuation_ext exists, owned by P1 as an extension table. TSD S1 v2 T3.1 names one table for the module, valuation (NEW). The Service Catalog states the resources of S1 with the §R9 placeholder.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: no row with owner S1. Architecture v5 slide 41: 'S1 / rwb-valuation / valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output / rwb_valuation / /cases/{id}/valuation'. TSD S1 v2 T3.1: '**valuation** (NEW). An appraisal of collateral or an asset.' Physical Schema v6: CREATE TABLE valuation_ext only.
Proposed fix: Add a valuation table (and the route decision record) to the Ownership Map v1 with owner S1, then to the Physical Schema rwb_valuation.sql; until then S1 records its resources with the §R9 placeholder.

Title: The Ownership Map v1 holds only proceeds for rwb-payment although Architecture v5 names fees, bookings and posting files
Detail: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P8 rwb-payment 'payment and proceeds matching, fees, bookings, posting files'. The Ownership Map v1 lists one table for P8, proceeds. TSD P8 v2 T3.1 also names payment_match_rule (NEW). No row in the Ownership Map v1 and no table in the Physical Schema v6 covers fees, bookings, posting files or payment_match_rule.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: P8 owns proceeds only. Architecture v5 slide 41 row P8. TSD P8 v2 T3.1: '**payment_match_rule** (NEW). A rule for matching a payment to a plan installment, by version.'
Proposed fix: Add the payment, fee, booking, posting-file and payment_match_rule tables to the Ownership Map v1 with owner P8 and to the Physical Schema rwb_payment.sql.

Title: The stack versions of the service template are not pinned in any source read for this work package
Detail: Architecture v5 names the parts of the service template (Spring Boot, outbox relay, inbox, Temporal worker, codec, OpenTelemetry, contract tests) and pins Temporal 1.30 or later and KEDA 2.17 or later for the scaler, but it pins no Spring Boot version, no Java runtime, no base image, no PostgreSQL driver and no Drools runtime. The Service Template Specification states the parts and carries the §R9 placeholder for the versions.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20: 'Every service: built from one template (Spring Boot, outbox relay, inbox, Temporal worker, codec, OpenTelemetry, contract tests).' Slide 38: 'Temporal 1.30+'. No version for the other parts appears in the read set.
Proposed fix: Pin the Spring Boot, Java runtime, base image, PostgreSQL driver and Drools versions in Wave 0 and record them in the template's version file and in the Environment and Deployment Design.

Title: Architecture v5 names a decision_record table in every service schema; the Ownership Map v1 has no row for it
Detail: Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service 'Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record', and slides 28 and 29 repeat that each service writes a local hash-linked decision record. The Ownership Map v1 carries outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key as PLT library objects but has no decision_record row. The Service Template Specification carries the §R9 placeholder for it.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20: 'DB Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record'. Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: no decision_record row; decision_log_entry is owned by P7 as the central ledger table.
Proposed fix: Add decision_record to the Ownership Map v1 as a PLT library object created in every service schema, and state its columns with the outbox and inbox tables.

Title: Temporal Schedule identifiers, calendars and overlap values are not defined
Detail: Ten live jobs become Temporal Schedules: JOB-06, JOB-10, JOB-14, JOB-16, JOB-17, JOB-18, JOB-19, JOB-20, JOB-21 and JOB-22. No source gives a Schedule ID, a cron expression, a Schedule-level overlap policy, a catch-up window or a time zone beyond the note that times are Asia/Bangkok. Times are stated as clock times or as cadence phrases: 'Daily 06:30', 'Daily 16:00', 'Nightly 02:00', 'Monthly, 3rd working day, on the ACE batch-complete record for ALS', 'Monthly, 1st Sunday', 'Every six months', 'Daily 00:01', 'Every 5 minutes', 'Daily 06:00'. Two of these cannot be written as a plain cron expression: JOB-16 must run on the third working day after AceDataReady, and JOB-17 runs on a weekday-dependent Sunday. The catalog and the design identify each Schedule by the job it serves and the name the source gives it, and carry the Schedule ID as the placeholder of Template and Rules R9.
Evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4, sheet Jobs, rows JOB-06 to JOB-22, column When, holds the times above and no identifier. Architecture v5 slide 44 notes read 'a Temporal Schedule (cron, with overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window)' with no value per job. Temporal and Drools design slide 12 lists 'Scheduled job' as an L3 kit template with no parameters. Ownership Map v1, sheet Jobs, column Replacement, names the mechanism and the owner of each job and no identifier.
Proposed fix: Confirm one Schedule ID per job in the owning service, the cron or calendar expression with the Asia/Bangkok time zone, the overlap policy, the catch-up window and the pause-on-failure rule; decide whether JOB-16 is a cron Schedule with an AceDataReady gate inside the workflow or an event-started run on the third working day.

Title: Activity timeouts, heartbeat intervals and task-queue limits are not specified
Detail: The design fixes the activity retry policy (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts) and the non-retryable NoPackageInForce failure, but no source gives a start-to-close timeout, a schedule-to-close timeout, a heartbeat interval or a task-queue rate limit for any activity. Architecture v5 slide 11 states only 'start-to-close per activity; backoff; heartbeats'. The rule evaluation target is under 300 ms and the agent run is capped at 60 s, and neither is written as an activity timeout. A worker that hangs therefore blocks its task until the workflow's default timeout, which is not stated either.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11, row Timeout, retry, column for the activity contract, reads 'Start-to-close per activity; backoff; heartbeats'. Temporal and Drools design slide 14 gives 'Retry policy: 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts; NoPackageInForce is non-retryable' and names no timeout. Slide 28 repeats the retry policy. Slide 32 item 6 lists Temporal 1.30+ and jobs as Schedules as the platform open points and says nothing about timeouts.
Proposed fix: Set a start-to-close timeout and a heartbeat interval per activity contract (EvaluateRules, RecordAndApply, the payment, document, partner, integration and reporting activities) and a task-queue rate limit per service, and publish them in the contract jar of each service.

Title: The event-started payment workflow of JOB-07 and JOB-08 has no name
Detail: Architecture v5 slide 44 makes JOB-07 payment matching and JOB-08 booking confirmation event-started workflows in rwb-payment, and the Temporal and Drools design names the activities matchPayments and confirmBookings that they run. No source names the workflow that hosts those activities, gives it a workflow ID or says whether one workflow hosts both jobs or each job has its own. The catalog lists both rows with the workflow name as the R9 placeholder and the activity as the only known step.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 rows JOB-07 and JOB-08 give the mechanism 'event-triggered workflow' with owner rwb-payment and no name. Slide 17 names 'Act: matchPayments, confirmBookings'. Temporal and Drools design slide 14 note reads 'rwb-payment's matchPayments activity (JOB-07, started by AceDataReady)', which names the activity and not the workflow.
Proposed fix: Name the workflow, its ID scheme (one run per business date and payment run key), and whether matchPayments and confirmBookings run in one workflow or two.

Title: The work started by six Schedules and three workflows is not named
Detail: Six of the ten target Schedules name neither the workflow nor the activity they start: rebalancing (JOB-06) is only 'Act: allocate, transfer, rebalance' on rwb-case; retention (JOB-17) only 'Schedule: retention' on rwb-document; access review list (JOB-18) only 'Schedule: access review list (six-monthly)' on rwb-access; re-appraisal (JOB-19) only 'Schedule: re-appraisal monthly' on rwb-asset; chain check (JOB-14) only 'Schedule: chain check 02:00' on rwb-decision; rule promote (JOB-20) is described in the v4 row text and publishes RulePackageInForce with no activity named. The two P1 workflows AceIngestCheck and reconciliation have no activity names either, the OCR, classify and extract steps of DocumentIntakeWorkflow are named as steps and not as activities, and the platform smoke workflow of JOB-22 is named with no statement of what it calls.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 TMP cells read 'Schedules: rule promote 00:01, chain check 02:00' and 'Act: allocate, transfer, rebalance'; slide 16 reads 'DocumentIntakeWorkflow: OCR, classify, extract; Act: generate, seal - Schedule: retention'; slide 44 gives the mechanism only. Batch and Scheduling Design v4 rows JOB-06 and JOB-14 to JOB-20 describe the work and no workflow. Temporal and Drools design slide 12 names the kit template 'Scheduled job' and no per-job content.
Proposed fix: Name the activity or workflow each Schedule starts, its input (business date or run key), its output and whether it is idempotent for a re-run of the same business date.

Title: Ten interaction-ledger features are listed in module P7 while the Ownership Map and DP-18 place the ledger with P1 rwb-source-data
Detail: All ten ledger features carry module P7: write every Workbench event to the ledger, hold the ledger beside the decision log, read it in one ordered sequence, reject a duplicate entry, raise an incident when it cannot be written, bring contact, dispatch and hand-over outcomes in, read the timeline on the case, and set the retention class. The R3 default ruling gives the interaction ledger to P1 rwb-source-data, DP-18 makes P1 the ledger owner, and the Ownership Map gives interaction and efs_ledger_outcome to P1 with ruling ASM-A6-tables-1, which keeps the case timeline and the interaction API with P3. FEAT-ILG-10 also touches retention, which the map gives to P5 rwb-document (retention_rule, ASM-A6-tables-10). The workbook has no owner column, so v5 cannot show the split; it keeps the module label and the Service column follows the module rule of CG-B-BIZ-36-1.
Evidence: FEAT-ILG-02: 'Hold the ledger beside the decision log', systems 'Workbench, ACE database', module P7, story keys N5. FEAT-ILG-06, 07 and 08 bring contact, dispatch and hand-over outcomes in (story key N4). Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: interaction owner P1, efs_ledger_outcome owner P1, both with ruling ASM-A6-tables-1. Template and Rules R3 default ruling table: 'Interaction ledger / P1 rwb-source-data'. DP-18: 'Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling)'.
Owner role: Solution architect of P1 rwb-source-data and of P7 rwb-decision
Proposed fix: Keep the ten features in P7 as the module that lists them and keep the Service column at P7 under the module rule. At story stage the ledger write, the store and the intake rule become P1 work through its contract and DP-18; the timeline on the case and the interaction API become P3 work; the retention class is applied through P5's retention contract. The Service Story Catalog records the split.

Title: Seven live features name the Data lake and Power BI as their systems, and INT-19 and INT-20 are removed
Detail: Seven live features publish into the data lake and Power BI: the daily reconciliation report, the baseline measures, the steering dashboard, the reporting baseline, the cross-source case count reconciliation, the measure refresh and the regulatory returns. DP-17 removes the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20 with it, and the target says reports come from rwb-reporting: Recovery has no data lake and no Power BI connection, and the extracts in JOB-15 run in rwb-reporting from its own projections. The seven rows still name a system that is no longer connected, so the delivery target of each row is undefined in the source.
Evidence: Systems column of the seven rows reads 'Power BI, Data lake'. Architecture v5 line 707: 'The data lake and Power BI are not connected (INT-19 and INT-20 removed).' Lines 2701 and 2703: 'Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20)' becomes 'Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'. Line 2296: 'measures 01:30 (rwb-reporting, JOB-15, from its own projections: no data lake)'. DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting; gap if the story needs lake data'.
Owner role: Reporting lead of P9 rwb-reporting and the solution architect of P1 rwb-source-data
Proposed fix: Keep the seven rows unchanged in v5. At story stage each read is taken from the rwb-reporting read model, built from events, and the extract is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-reporting (JOB-15). No feed to the data lake and no Power BI connection is built; if a story truly needs lake data it raises its own gap under DP-17.

Title: CTL-36 first runs in E5 while its owner service rwb-partner is wave 4
Detail: CTL-36, partner service levels and recoverable court fees, states First in E5. EP05 is wave 3 in the R5.6 wave map, while S9 rwb-partner, the service that owns panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees and scorecards, is created in wave 4. Version 4 keeps First in E5 word for word, records S9 rwb-partner as the owner service and raises this conflict. The other 43 controls map to a service whose wave is at or before the wave of their first release.
Evidence: Controls CTL-36 column First in reads E5. Template and Rules R5.6: EP04 and EP05 are wave 3. Architecture v5 slide 41: S9 rwb-partner, wave 4. Ownership Map sheet Services: S9 rwb-partner, wave 4. Architecture v5 slide 17: InstructionWorkflow with SLA timers; S9 owns fees and scorecards; JOB-18 and JOB-19 are the only Temporal Schedules outside rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-writeoff and rwb-payment.
Proposed fix: Decide whether CTL-36 runs from wave 3 on partner instructions and fee data published by S9 through its contract and fake, or whether its first release moves to E6, where S9 rwb-partner exists; record the ruling in the Change Register.

Title: The conduct sample control has no owner in the Ownership Map
Detail: CTL-39 checks a monthly sample of contacts, notices and decisions against the conduct rules and names the Conduct and QA officer as the performer. The Ownership Map has no conduct, QA sample or sample object, endpoint, event, workflow or job, so no service is fixed for it. Version 4 records P9 rwb-reporting, derived from the measures, snapshots and regulatory reports it owns and from the all-business-events projection, because the sample reads notices, interactions and decisions from events.
Evidence: Controls CTL-39 columns Performed by and How it is tested: Conduct and QA officer; re-perform a sample; monthly. Ownership Map sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs contain no conduct or sample row. Architecture v5 slide 41: P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard and regulatory reports. Slide 15: rwb-reporting receives all business events as projections.
Proposed fix: Confirm P9 rwb-reporting as owner of the conduct sample, or add the sample as a P9 measure and a P4 rwb-access review, and record the ruling in the Ownership Map before E8.

Title: Scores (DP11) have no owning schema and no table
Detail: The source gives Scores (DP11) a 2-year period and a delete action but names no store. No table in the Physical Schema v6 carries DP11 and no service schema is named for it; the only read is the ACE view v_ace_score through the ACE view contract.
Evidence: Physical Schema v6: no table with data product DP11; Logical Data Model v8 LOV-DATA-PRODUCT DP11 Scores and route economics and DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 v_ace_score; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 for the P1 ACE view contract.
Proposed fix: Name the record against the read that supplies it, v_ace_score through rwb-source-data, keep the 2-year delete period, and let the ACE owner apply it.

Title: No operation or event lets the retention job act on another service's schema
Detail: The source has one monthly job that lists, reviews, approves and destroys records. Retention is owned by P5 rwb-document, but the rows sit in 19 schemas and no service may write another service's tables. Neither the API Specification nor the Event and Messaging Design has an expiry or destroy operation or event.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 ruling: retention is P5 rwb-document; plan DP-01 and ADR-014: one schema per service, no cross-schema reads or writes; API Specification v4 and Event and Messaging Design v4: no retention or expiry path.
Proposed fix: Let the owner of each schema act on its own rows, and let the P5 decision reach it over that service's REST contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout, until an expiry event is added to the catalog.

Title: Consent state table and column name in the target schema
Detail: Consent state is cited as contact_point.consent_status, a monolith table name. The target table is contact_point_ext in rwb_source_data (Ownership Map v1), but the column name is not stated in any source, so the citation cannot be resolved to a column.
Evidence: v2 section 3 first bullet: (contact_point.consent_status); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: contact_point_ext owner P1, schema rwb_source_data.
Proposed fix: Read the consent state as a column of rwb_source_data.contact_point_ext and carry the exact column name to the P1 DB and API stories when the P1 design fixes it.

Title: Debt sale tape masking check has no owner and no field list
Detail: The design requires a masking check on a debt sale tape to the sale terms, but states neither which service selects the fields nor which service performs the check. The per-sale field list is not in the sources.
Evidence: v2 section 4 fourth bullet and section 8 second row; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-debtsale the lots and data room and rwb-integration the buyer file (INT-25); Ownership Map v1 gives debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account to S6.
Proposed fix: S6 rwb-debtsale selects the fields to the sale terms and P2 rwb-integration performs the check at delivery; the per-sale field list comes from the sale terms, not from this design.

Title: Tokenization point and token format are not stated
Detail: National ID and passport numbers are tokenized at load, but the sources do not state which component mints the token, whether the token is reversible, or its format. The load is rwb-source-data (P1), which is the only service that reads the ACE views.
Evidence: v2 section 4 first bullet; Architecture v5 slides 7 and 15 (rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_* only); Ownership Map v1 gives the extension tables to P1.
Proposed fix: P1 mints the token at load and stores no clear value; the token format and any detokenization path are fixed in the P1 design and the access profile of P4.

Title: No entity is owned by S1 rwb-valuation, although Architecture v5 gives S1 the valuations and the route decision
Detail: The Ownership Map assigns 93 tables to 18 services and the platform library. rwb-valuation owns none of them: the appraisal data is the read-only v_ace_valuation view and valuation_ext, both P1 under the map's own ruling, and the assets are S5. S1 therefore has no table, no schema content and no DB story of its own in this model, although Arch v5 gives it 'valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output'.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: no row with owner S1; rows valuation_ext (owner P1) and listing and asset_sale (owner S5); Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings row valuation_ext (ruling ASM-A6-tables-15 keeps valuation_ext with P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (S1 rwb-valuation owning valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output); v6 Entities rows Valuation extension and v_ace_valuation.
Proposed fix: Record S1 as owning no entity in this version and let its DB story create the rwb_valuation schema with its Flyway baseline only; refer the definition of a rwb_valuation table, if one is wanted, to the S1 design review.

Title: The inventory has no rule for events, workflow inputs or logs
Detail: The inventory classifies storage, screens, prompts, test data, export and the debt sale tape, but it has no rule for a Kafka event, a Temporal workflow input or history, or an application log. Those are the three channels the realignment must close, so every field carries no statement about what may leave the service.
Evidence: v4 Handling B5 to B22 (Where values: Stored, On screen, In logs, In agent prompts, In test data, Export, Debt sale tape, Retention, Data subject request, In ACE, Contact values, Every ACE read) has no row for an event or a workflow; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 833 (Never: personal data in events, I/O or PII in workflow code or payloads), line 1618 (Payload: IDs and business facts, no PII), line 3064 and Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 1885 (payload codec, search attributes); Template and Rules R7.2 s17.
Proposed fix: Three appended columns on Fields and Identifiers, six new Handling rows and a new PII controls sheet give the rule per field and per channel, with the owner of each control.

Title: No source names the 19 service repositories, their source-control group or the way an empty repository is provisioned
Detail: The realignment gives every service its own repository, created from the service template of RWB-PLT-TPL, with one code owners file in each. No source read for this document gives a repository name, a group or project in the bank source control, or the provisioning route, so version 6 states the rule and names each repository after its service until the convention is stated.
Evidence: Template and Rules R5.1: 'RWB-PLT-TPL: service template and repositories'; Architecture v5 slide 38 note: 'one Helm chart, one golden pipeline'; the v5 document names 'one repository' only, with no name; Architecture v5 names no repository, group or project and no source-control product beyond the Helm chart and pipeline statements. The Ownership Map v1 Services sheet gives service, schema, REST base, topic and queue but no repository.
Proposed fix: State the repository naming convention and the source-control group, provision the 19 empty repositories with branch protection and a code owners file from the service template, and add the repository name to the Services sheet of the Ownership Map.

Title: The four DEV and two SIT deployment slots of version 5 are not stated per service now that there are 19 services with an api and a worker each
Detail: Version 5 counts four planned DEV slots and two SIT slots for one deployable. The realignment deploys about 38 small deployments, one api and one worker per service, so the slot count per service and the way a later wave gets a slot are not stated. Version 6 keeps the four and two figures of version 5, keeps DL35, and leaves the per-service slot model open rather than inventing one.
Evidence: Version 5 section 7: 'ACE has four deployment slots planned in DEV and two in SIT, so squads can test in parallel. One slot in each is available today; the rest are being provisioned (DL35)'; Architecture v5 slide 49 note: 'about 38 small deployments at rest (most workers idle at minimum)'; no source read gives a slot per service or a wave-to-slot rule.
Proposed fix: Publish the per-service deployment slot plan for DEV and SIT with the wave each service starts in, and replace the four and two figures with that plan when it exists.

Title: No source states who approves a published contract version or where the contract artefact is held for its consumers
Detail: The realignment makes the contract the first thing a service publishes, and a change that is not backward compatible takes a new version and an ADR. No source read states who approves a contract version, how a consumer is told that a new version exists, or where the published OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and contract jar are held. Version 6 records the contract in the Service Contract Catalog v1 and in the service's API Specification file as the run material and leaves approval and publication open.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11: 'Every service publishes its contracts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, activity jar) before code; contract tests run in every build'; Template and Rules R8.4 lists 'Service Contract Catalog v1' and 'API Specification split into 19 files plus gateway-bff and an index' as run outputs; no source read names a contract approver, a review step or a published artefact store.
Proposed fix: Name the contract approver role and the artefact store, add a contract review step to the CON story, and record the approved version in the Service Contract Catalog.

Title: The Ownership Map v1 gives rwb-valuation no table, so its schema and its first migration have no listed content
Detail: Every service runs its own Flyway sequence in its own schema, so each service needs at least a baseline. The Tables sheet of the Ownership Map v1 has no row for S1 rwb-valuation, while it gives S1 three REST operations and a workflow; under the per-service Flyway rule the service would own no table. Version 6 states that its schema starts with its baseline only and leaves the ownership of a valuation table open.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: 87 table rows, none with owner S1; sheet Endpoints: three rows with owner S1; sheet Workflows and activities: RouteDecisionWorkflow with owner S1; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-valuation the schema rwb_valuation and slide 19 gives it the valuation and route service, with no table list; Template and Rules R5.7 rule 7 requires every service to have a contract story, not a table.
Proposed fix: Decide whether rwb-valuation keeps a table of its own, for example a route decision or valuation snapshot table, and add the row to the Tables sheet and to the rwb_valuation.sql file.

Title: Version 4 has no delivery wave, and Architecture v5 puts Epics 2 and 3 in one wave while the plan gives each epic its own monthly release
Detail: Version 4 is a release calendar only: eight monthly releases, one per epic, with no wave. Architecture v5 slide 38 sets four service waves plus Wave 0, and states Wave 2 as Epics 2-3, Wave 3 as Epics 4-5 and Wave 4 as Epics 6-7, so a wave spans two or three monthly releases while the plan releases once a month. Template and Rules R5.6 maps business epics to waves the same way (EP01 to 1, EP02 and EP03 to 2, EP04 and EP05 to 3, EP06 to EP08 to 4). No source read states which release starts a wave or how a wave boundary is written on a monthly release, so version 5 states the boundary as the first release of the wave's first epic and records the position here.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38: 'Wave 1 - Epic 1', 'Wave 2 - Epics 2-3', 'Wave 3 - Epics 4-5', 'Wave 4 - Epics 6-7' and note 'Waves follow the first epic of each module'; Template and Rules R5.6 gives the same map by business epic; Release Plan v4 Releases sheet holds one row per epic E1 to E8 with one release date each and no wave column; Release Plan v4 Calendar sheet holds the same eight epics with no wave.
Proposed fix: Confirm that a wave starts at the first release of its first epic (Wave 2 at E2, Wave 3 at E4, Wave 4 at E6) and keep the eight monthly releases with their dates; if the programme instead releases once per wave, E2 and E3 merge and the calendar is rewritten.

Title: The plan has no Wave 0 row and no platform release, so nothing states when the platform enablers are complete
Detail: Architecture v5 makes Wave 0 the enabler: service template, Helm chart, contract libraries, workflow kit, 19 schemas and logins, Kafka topics and ACLs and Temporal 1.30+, all before Wave 1. Version 4 has no platform release and no Wave 0 row: its first release is E1 on 30 November 2026 and its gates G1 to G6 are all per release. No source read gives a date by which Wave 0 must be complete, so version 5 states it as the E1 go decision, 27 November 2026, taken from the E1 row of the plan, and records the position here rather than inventing a platform release.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38: 'Wave 0 - now. Platform once. Service template + Helm, Contract libraries, Workflow kit (L3), 19 schemas + logins, Kafka topics + ACLs, Temporal 1.30+'; Template and Rules R5.1 lists seven platform epics RWB-PLT-TPL to RWB-PLT-OBS; Release Plan v4 Releases sheet first data row is E1 with build start 2 November 2026, go decision 27 November 2026 and release 30 November 2026; the plan's Gates sheet has no platform or wave gate.
Proposed fix: Add a Wave 0 row to the plan with its own entry and exit criteria, owned by the platform epics of R5.1, and confirm that Wave 0 completes before the E1 go decision.

Title: No source states who approves a published contract or that a release gate covers contract publication
Detail: Architecture v5 requires every service to publish its OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and activity contracts with a fake before code, and Template and Rules R5.4 makes a contract dependency (class C) non-blocking, which only works if a published contract exists. Version 4 has six gates per release and none of them covers contract publication, and no source read names the role that approves a contract version or the artefact where it is published. Version 5 adds gate G7 Contract published, decided by the code owner of the owning service with the solution architect, and records the missing approval route here.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11: 'Every service publishes its contracts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, activity jar) before code; contract tests run in every build'; Template and Rules R5.4 class C: 'Build against the published contract and its fake. Blocks the build? No'; Template and Rules R5.7 rules 1 and 2 make a CON story Day 1; Release Plan v4 Gates sheet holds G1 Design signed to G6 Benefit check only; no source read names a contract approver or a contract artefact store.
Proposed fix: Name the contract approver role and the artefact store, then confirm gate G7 with that role as its decider and cite it from every CON story of the wave.

Title: Version 4 gives S4 rwb-litigation notice approval in E2 while Architecture v5 creates S4 in Wave 3
Detail: The E2 row of version 4 lists 'S4 notice approval' and the Modules by release sheet gives S4 'E2 notices; E5', so the E2 release needs part of rwb-litigation. Architecture v5 slide 38 creates S4 in Wave 3 with Epics 4-5, and slide 41 puts rwb-litigation in wave 3. Template and Rules R5.6 resolves a story whose business-epic wave is earlier than its service's wave in favour of the business epic and asks for one conflict gap per service and business epic, which is this row. Version 5 keeps the E2 content of the source unchanged, marks S4 as a Wave 3 service with E2 work, and records the position here.
Evidence: Release Plan v4 Releases sheet E2 Modules and content: 'S4 notice approval'; Modules by release sheet S4: 'E2 notices; E5'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 38 'Wave 3 - Epics 4-5: S1 Valuation, S3 Guarantee, S4 Litigation, S6 Debt sale' and slide 41 gives S4 rwb-litigation wave 3; Template and Rules R5.6: 'A story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service's Arch v5 wave keeps the W-MAP wave. One conflict gap is raised per service and business epic.'
Proposed fix: Either bring the S4 service creation forward to Wave 2 so that E2 notice approval has a service, or move the E2 notice approval to E5 and keep S4 in Wave 3; record the choice in the Decision Log against DL44 and DL48.

Title: Only the first release date is named; the Wave 2, 3 and 4 release dates and the wave to release mapping are not stated
Detail: Version 3 plans one monthly release and names the first release, 30 November 2026. Architecture v5 splits delivery into five waves and names no wave date, and no source read for this document says which monthly release carries Wave 2, Wave 3 or Wave 4. Version 4 therefore marks the Wave 1 release as 30 November 2026 (tentative) and writes the placeholder for the other three dates rather than inventing them.
Evidence: Version 3 section 1: 'The first release, 30 November 2026, also starts the case list'; Architecture v5 slide 38 gives Wave 0 to Wave 4 and their services with no date; slide 38 note: 'BOT approval before Wave 1 go-live, if required (FPG 19/2560 cl. 5.5; up to 30 business days)'; the version 3 open decisions list DL34 (the release window) only.
Proposed fix: Publish the release calendar with one date per wave, add it to DL34, and replace the placeholder of section 10.1 with the dates; keep every date marked tentative.

Title: No source states that one wave goes live per release or how a wave maps to a release
Detail: Version 3 releases one deployable a month, so a release and a release scope are the same thing. The realignment has 19 services in four delivery waves and one platform wave, and no source read for this document states whether a wave is one release, whether two waves can share a release, or which services of a wave go live together. Version 4 assumes one wave per release and adds the cutover order inside a wave; both are recorded as assumptions.
Evidence: Version 3 section 2 describes one deploy of 'the tag' per release; Architecture v5 slide 38 shows Wave 0 to Wave 4 with the service count per wave and no release number; Template and Rules R5.6 gives the business-epic wave map and no release identifier.
Proposed fix: State one wave per release in the release calendar, together with the order of services inside a wave, and keep both under change control with DL34.

Title: The first-release scope is written per capability, not per service, so the Wave 1 service that delivers each capability is not stated
Detail: Version 3 lists the first-release scope as case list, ACE views, spreadsheets, access, documents and tracker retirement, which are capabilities of one deployable. In the realignment each capability belongs to a named service, and the source gives no mapping. Version 4 adds the service to each row of section 7 and a services row naming the nine Wave 1 services, taken from the Ownership Map and the Architecture v5 contracts.
Evidence: Version 3 section 7 rows: Case list, ACE views, Spreadsheets, Access, Documents; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 give the owner of each capability (case list in rwb-case, access in rwb-access, documents in rwb-document, notices in rwb-comms); Ownership Map v1 Services sheet gives the nine Wave 1 services.
Proposed fix: Walk through the first-release scope with the nine Wave 1 service owners before the rehearsal, and record the owning service for each capability in section 7.

Title: The rollback of version 3 switches one set of feature flags and redeploys one tag, and has no per-service rollback, no Worker Versioning statement and no rule package rollback
Detail: Version 3 rolls back one deployable: flags off, then the previous tag, then the previous reference data. With 19 services a wave is 2 to 9 independent deployments with in-flight Temporal cases and versioned rule packages, and no source read states how a single service is rolled back without touching the rest of the wave, how an in-flight case keeps its build, or how a rule package is reverted. Version 4 writes the per-service rollback from the Temporal and Drools design and records the change here.
Evidence: Version 3 section 4: 'Switch the feature flags for the release off', 'redeploy the previous tag', 'Reload the previous reference data versions'; Architecture v5 slide 23 rules: 'Kit versioned; workers pinned (Worker Versioning)' and 'Continue-As-New at stage ends'; Temporal and Drools design T4: rollback of a rule package is one call, with states ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED.
Proposed fix: Add a per-service rollback rehearsal to the UAT rehearsal of every wave, and record the previous tag and the previous rule package version in the release checklist.

Title: Version 3 has the release read the 30 views under a recovery role, while Architecture v5 gives the views to rwb-source-data only, one login per service
Detail: Version 3 says the Workbench reads the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views and checks that 'the recovery role reads recovery.v_ace_* only'. Architecture v5 gives the views to rwb-source-data alone, with the login rwb_source_data, and every other service reads ACE data through that service's contract. Architecture v5 wins on source precedence, so version 4 keeps the 30 views and the 21 ACE tables and changes the login and the reader; the loser is recorded here.
Evidence: Version 3 section 1: 'the release reads the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views (D-RCV-35, ADR-010)'; section 6: 'the recovery role reads recovery.v_ace_* only'; Architecture v5 slide 29: 'rwb-source-data, login rwb_source_data, recovery.v_ace_* views: SELECT only' and 'only rwb_source_data has SELECT on the views'.
Proposed fix: Change the production grant to the rwb_source_data login, drop every other reader, and re-run the conformance test of the 80 appendix fields under that login before the Wave 1 rehearsal.

Title: No source states the production capacity or the deployment slot model for a wave of up to nine services
Detail: Version 3 deploys one tag into one production slot. Wave 1 is nine services, each an api and a worker deployment, so a cutover night deploys 18 deployments and the cluster holds about 38 at rest. No source read for this document gives a production slot count, a per-service cluster request or a wave capacity check, so version 4 states the deployment per service and leaves the capacity position open rather than inventing a number.
Evidence: Version 3 section 2: 'Deploy the tag to production in the change window', one row; Architecture v5 slide 8: '19 services in the rwb-recovery namespace, each an api and a worker deployment'; slide 49 note: 'about 38 small deployments at rest (most workers idle at minimum)'; no source read gives a production capacity figure.
Proposed fix: Publish the production capacity and slot plan per wave with the cluster requests of each service, and add the capacity check to section 10.2 step 2 when it exists.

Title: Version 2 gives four severity bands but no alert threshold, no SLO and no dashboard per service
Detail: Version 2 fixes a respond time and a restore time for four severities and nothing else. A run book per service needs the signal that starts the clock on that service: an error rate, a consumer lag, a dead-letter count or an outbox age. Architecture v5 gives the health and metrics endpoints, the retry topics and the dead-letter alert, and ADR-023 makes observability per service, but no source read gives a threshold, an error budget or a dashboard per service, so version 3 uses the four severity bands and leaves the threshold open.
Evidence: Version 2 slide 3 gives respond and restore times only, with no threshold; Architecture v5 slide 20: 'REST /health, /metrics for the platform'; slide 22: 'retry topics 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, then .dlt + alert'; no source read gives an alert threshold, an SLO, an error budget or a named dashboard for any of the 19 services.
Proposed fix: Publish one alert and dashboard page per service, with latency, error rate, consumer lag, dead-letter count and outbox age, and cite it from the service's run book page.

Title: No source gives an on-call rota per service or the hand-off from the tier roles to the 19 services
Detail: Version 2 has business hours with tier 1 and tier 2 on duty, an early shift for the data steward and outside hours with SCB IT on call for severity 1 and the platform administrator on call by rota. It gives one rota for one deployable. The target has 19 services in waves 1 to 4, so the rota and the hand-off point from tier 1 to the service concerned have to be stated per service. No source read for this deck states either, so version 3 keeps the four rows of version 2 and adds the per-service column with the open value.
Evidence: Version 2 slide 4: 'Outside hours / SCB IT on call for severity 1; platform administrator on call by rota'; slide 5 gives four escalation rows and no rota; the Services sheet of the Ownership Map v1 gives the wave of each of the 19 services but no rota; no source read names a paging tool, a rota period or a hand-off point.
Proposed fix: Publish one rota page per service for business hours, the early shift and outside hours, and state the point at which tier 1 hands a request to the service's owner.

Title: The DevOps team type has no full-time equivalent in the resource plan
Detail: Template and Rules R5.3 makes the DevOps team the suggested owner of every OPS story, and the plan has OPS stories in every wave (the pipeline, Helm chart, KEDA scaling, outbox relay, worker deployments and observability). The Team and People by month sheets have no DevOps row and the Total row counts none.
Evidence: Team sheet: 24 rows, no DevOps role; People by month sheet: 20 role rows, none DevOps; the Total row of that sheet sums the 20 rows to 29.5.
Proposed fix: Add the DevOps full-time equivalents to the plan of the next version, or state that the pipeline work is carried by the TechX squads. The sheet records 0 and the placeholder instead of inventing a number.

Title: SCB IT infrastructure has no full-time equivalent and appears only as a shared supporting team
Detail: Template and Rules R5.3 makes SCB IT infrastructure the suggested owner of every INF story (AKS namespace, Kafka topic ACLs and quotas, Temporal namespace quotas, keys and certificates, the network path to ACE). The Structure sheet names 'SCB IT security, architecture team' under supporting teams and the People by month sheet does not count them.
Evidence: Structure sheet row 'Supporting teams: Data engineering, Enterprise AI, Autonomous Ops, SCB IT security, architecture team'; People by month note 'Shared teams are not counted'.
Proposed fix: Confirm the infrastructure capacity as a shared service with named working agreements per wave; the plan records the placeholder, not a number.

Title: The daily copy of the decision log to the data lake and its row-count reconciliation have no target under Architecture v5
Detail: REQ-DRI-009 requires the decision log to be copied to the data lake daily with row counts matched, and the FSD builds that copy as FEAT-DRI-06 with JOB-13 at 01:00, a watermark, a manifest and check REC-08. Architecture v5 removes the data lake (ADR-018): reporting reads events into rwb-reporting, JOB-13 keeps its ID with 'ingest is continuous (Kafka)', and DP-17 records the lake as removed. The requirement therefore has no target and no consumer, and its acceptance criteria describe a store that will not exist. A PRD that kept it would create a backlog item for removed infrastructure.
Evidence: FSD P7 A2.6 AC-P7-006-01 reads 'the data lake copy has the same row count and the same last hash as the live log'; TSD P7 T5.1 lists INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI' and INT-20; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-13 reads 'Decision log copy / 01:00 / rwb-decision / ingest is continuous (Kafka)'; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 reads 'Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 / Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting'.
Owner role: Solution architect with the reporting and BI analyst
Proposed fix: Retire REQ-DRI-009 with RWB-E1-014 (already recorded as retired in the Change Register) and re-issue FSD P7 without FEAT-DRI-06 and its acceptance criteria; record in the P9 PRD that reporting reads DecisionRecorded into its own read model, and keep the population query of this service as the audit path.

Title: FSD P9 has no requirement IDs, so FR rows cannot map to FSD REQ IDs
Detail: The 'Requirements served' table of FSD P9 is present and empty. The FSD carries feature IDs (FEAT-RPT-01 to FEAT-RPT-10) and acceptance criteria IDs (AC-P9-xxx) but no REQ- IDs. The work package asks for FR rows mapped to FSD REQ IDs; there are none to map to, so every FR row names the FSD feature and acceptance criterion it comes from instead.
Evidence: FSD P9 'Requirements served' table with a header and no rows; A1.2 feature overview; A2.1 to A2.10
Proposed fix: Trace FR rows to FEAT-RPT-nn and AC-P9-nnn-nn; add REQ IDs to the FSD if a program-level key is needed

Title: JOB-15 is described both as a Temporal Schedule at 01:30 and as an Airflow trigger
Detail: Slide 15 gives rwb-reporting 'Temporal Schedule: measures 01:30' together with 'Act: buildRegulatoryExtract'. Slide 44 gives JOB-15 as 'Airflow trigger (no data lake)' at 01:30, and slide 31 note 3 sends the report and regulatory extract through POST /v1/reports/{id}/run. Batch and Scheduling Design v4 writes the extract to the data lake nightly. Three mechanisms are named for one job.
Evidence: Arch v5 slide 15 IN line; slide 31 note 3; slide 44 JOB-15; Ownership Map ruling on JOB-15
Owner role: Solution architect with the bank platform team
Proposed fix: Build the schedule at 01:30 and the run operation as the same run's two entries, and let the owner pick the live path

Title: The report resource path differs between the architecture and the ownership map
Detail: Arch v5 gives P9 the resources GET /dashboards/{id}, GET /reports/{id} and POST /reports/{id}/run. The Ownership Map and API Specification v4 carry GET /reports/measures. It is not stated what value {id} takes, or whether the measure read is a separate resource from the report read.
Evidence: Arch v5 slide 15 IN line and slide 41 catalogue row P9 (/dashboards/{id}); Ownership Map api entry 'GET /reports/measures'
Proposed fix: Keep both paths in the contract, read /reports/{id} as /reports/measures for the measure report, and confirm the identifier

Title: No field catalog exists for the snapshot, the publication, the report definition, the run record or the projections
Detail: The FSD gives one field catalog of eight fields, and it is the measure_definition catalog repeated in three sections. measure_snapshot, measure_publish, the report and return definitions, the extract run record and the read-model projections have no field list beyond the attributes named in the acceptance criteria.
Evidence: FSD P9 A2.3.3.2, A2.6.3.2, A2.9.3.2 (the same eight measure_definition fields); the acceptance criteria name business_date, definition_version, freshness stamp and row count only
Proposed fix: Carry the named attributes in this PRD and take the rest from the technical specification and the logical data model

Title: Seven module specifications still send extracts and copies to a data lake that Architecture v5 removes
Detail: FSD P1 carries FEAT-RDF-20 'Copy the decision log to the lake', FSD P7 carries FEAT-DRI-06 'Stream the decision log to the data lake', FSD P2 carries INT-19 and INT-20 as outbound files to the data lake and COLLINS through the data lake, and FSD P4, P6, P9 and P10 name the data lake copy in requirements, integration points and ACs. Architecture v5 has no data lake: reporting reads events into `rwb-reporting` (DP-17, ADR-018), and Template and Rules R6 retires RWB-E1-014. Version 7 keeps every extract and AC word for word and records the position in the Architecture v5 note of each affected module.
Evidence: FSD P1 v3 FEAT-RDF-20; FSD P7 v3 FEAT-DRI-06; FSD P2 v3 A1.5 INT-19 and INT-20 and 'In scope'; FSD P6 v3 'Integration points. Power BI, Data lake'; FSD P9 v3 'Integration points. Power BI, Data lake'; FSD P4 v3 REQ-ACA-006; FSD P10 v3 AC-EXC-P10-006-01; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17, R6 retired row RWB-E1-014; ADR-018
Proposed fix: The data-lake extracts and their ACs are removed at the next FSD baseline and replaced by the event-fed `rwb-reporting` read model; until then the notes and the story set carry the position, and no story builds a lake copy.

Title: Five module specifications name the Quartz scheduler as their scheduling mechanism
Detail: FSD P3, S1, S4 and S8 give 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler' as their integration points, and FSD P7 carries AC-EXC-P7-014-01, which adds a Quartz job JOB-12. Architecture v5 replaces Quartz with Temporal Schedules and event-started workflows through the workflow kit (DP-10, ADR-016), and Template and Rules R6 retires RWB-TE-007. Version 7 keeps the wording word for word and records the position in the Architecture v5 note of each affected module.
Evidence: FSD P3 v4, S1 v3, S4 v3 and S8 v3 'Integration points. Workbench, Quartz scheduler'; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-014-01 (Quartz job JOB-12); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-10 and R6 retired row RWB-TE-007; ADR-016
Proposed fix: At the next FSD baseline the Quartz integration points and the JOB-12 AC become Temporal Schedules and event-started workflows on the owning service's task queue; the story set already builds the schedules through RWB-PLT-E1071.

Title: 'Weeks' versus '28 days' wording for the same period
Detail: The NFR set and the design set use two wordings for the same period: 'weeks' for a wait or a retention, and '28 days'. The retention requirements give no period at all (NFR-028 'periods not set', NFR-031 and NFR-075 'Not set', decision DL26), and the only 28 days in the realignment sources is the Temporal Continue-As-New interval of the workflow design, not a retention period. Version 4 keeps every target word for word and states the reading in the section 3.5 note, so a reader does not take 28 days as a retention period.
Evidence: NFR-028 target 'Retention classes defined per type; periods not set'; NFR-030, NFR-031 and NFR-075 targets and decision DL26; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13 'Continue-As-New at each stage end, at least every 28 days'; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-011 option text 'A wait of weeks is a row with a state and a stored due date'
Proposed fix: Compliance states each retention period in one unit for the document types, the decision log, the case records and the interaction ledger, and the 28 days stays only in the workflow design as the Continue-As-New interval

Title: The shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 has no topic settings
Detail: Every service publishes DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1 and rwb-decision consumes it into the central ledger within five minutes. No source gives the partitions, replication factor, retention, key, schema subject or ACLs of that topic; the per-service topics rwb.<short>.events.v1 carry 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention and key caseId on slide 9 of the same extract, and those settings are not stated for the shared topic.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 lists rwb.<name>.events.v1 for each of the 19 services and names rwb.decision-record.v1 only in slide 20 ('DecisionRecorded -> rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)') and slide 28 ('rwb-decision reads rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger within 5 minutes'). Slide 9 gives the Kafka settings for the service topics only. Rules R4 names the shared topic and no settings.
Proposed fix: Set the partitions, replication factor, retention, key, subject naming and ACLs of rwb.decision-record.v1 with the Kafka platform team, and publish them with the topic catalogue.

Title: A service's first epic in version 6 differs from its wave in Architecture v5
Detail: Version 6 slide 15 attributes features to epics: P8 matching in E2 and posting in E4, S2 foundations in E2 and settlement in E3, S5 record in E3 and auction in E4, S4 notices in E2 and end to end in E5, S6 data in E5 and screens in E6, S8 screening in E2 and end to end in E7, S7 in E6, S9 panel in E6 and scoring in E7, S1 and S3 in E4. Architecture v5 slide 38 and the Ownership Map give one wave per service: P8, S2, S5 and S8 in wave 2, S1, S3, S4 and S6 in wave 3, S7 and S9 in wave 4. A service therefore first appears in a different epic under the two readings, which changes the wave a story belongs to and the wave band of the diagram.
Evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 15, column Added, reads for E2 'P8 matching skeleton ... S2 treatment record; S4 notice approval; S8 deviation screening', for E3 'S5 asset record ...', for E4 'S1 route decision ... S3 guarantee ... S5 auction rounds ... P8 posting', for E5 'S4 litigation end to end ... S6 lot data and data room', for E6 'S6 debt sale screens ... S7 write-off ... S9 partner panel'. Architecture v5 slide 38 gives 'Wave 2 · Epics 2-3 +4 services P8, S2, S5, S8' and 'Wave 3 · Epics 4-5 +4 services S1, S3, S4, S6'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services gives wave 2 to P8, S2, S5, S8; wave 3 to S1, S3, S4, S6; wave 4 to S7, S9.
Proposed fix: Resolve in favour of the Architecture v5 wave map (R-PREC 1): the wave of a service is the Ownership Map wave; version 6 slide 15 keeps the features each epic adds and the deck states that a service's wave, not its epic of first use, fixes its delivery band.

Title: No source sizes the deployment slots for 38 deployments across four environments
Detail: Version 6 counts slots per environment: DEV four planned and one available, SIT two planned and one available (DL35), UAT shared with the collection squad, PROD on the shared ACE AKS clusters. Architecture v5 makes each of the 19 services an api and a worker deployment, about 38 deployments at rest, plus Temporal, Kafka clients, the gateway and observability. No source states whether the planned slots hold 38 deployments per environment, how the namespaces and quotas are split between the environments, or when the missing slots arrive.
Evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 14 rows DEV and SIT read 'Four slots planned, one available (DL35)' and 'Two slots planned, one available (DL35)'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes read 'about 38 small deployments at rest (most workers idle at minimum), one Helm chart and one pipeline template'. Slide 38 makes wave 0 the enabler with the template, the Helm chart and the 19 schemas and logins. No slide gives a slot count for the target.
Proposed fix: Confirm the slots and quotas per environment for 38 deployments plus the platform components, and record the date each missing slot arrives against wave 0.

Title: S1 owns the valuations but has no table in the Ownership Map
Detail: T3.1 of TSD S1 defines the valuation table as a NEW table of S1, and Architecture v5 slide 41 says rwb-valuation owns the valuations. The Ownership Map Tables sheet lists no table owned by S1 (valuation_ext is P1's), while its Endpoints sheet gives S1 the two valuation paths.
Evidence: Ownership Map Endpoints ruling POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations (owner S1, ASM-A6-api-6); Tables sheet: no S1 row; Arch v5 slide 41: rwb-valuation owns the valuations.
Proposed fix: Create rwb_valuation with the valuation and route decision tables of T3.1, and keep valuation_ext with P1 as the SVAF extension table.

Title: The Arch v5 contract paths and the published OpenAPI files differ
Detail: The Arch v5 contract slides name operations that the published per-service files do not carry on the same path, for example S1 /cases/{id}/route-proposals against the published POST /cases/{caseId}/route, and P3 /cases/{id}/actions, GET /tasks and GET /case-summary/{id} against the published /me/tasks and PATCH /tasks/{taskId}.
Evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (S1 IN) and slide 14 (P3 IN) against rwb-valuation.yaml and rwb-case.yaml.
Proposed fix: Take the published OpenAPI file as the contract and raise the Arch v5 wording as a correction to the architecture pack.

Title: No interface carries the reporting output after INT-19 and INT-20 are removed
Detail: Version 3 names INT-19 (case, queue, decision and outcome data to the data lake and Power BI, nightly) and INT-20 (decisions and outcomes to COLLINS for model learning, nightly) as the only reporting and model-learning outbound interfaces, both owned by the Workbench and retried in the next window. Architecture v5 has no data lake and DP-17 removes both rows: reporting becomes a read model in rwb-reporting built from events, JOB-13 becomes continuous Kafka ingest in rwb-decision and JOB-15 becomes an Airflow trigger. No source then names the interface that delivers the rwb-reporting read model to Power BI or to a regulator, or the interface that carries decision records to the model owner for learning, so version 4 removes the two rows and adds no replacement. Without an interface the reporting story has an output nobody receives, and the model-learning need of COLLINS has no path at all.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-19 / Data lake and Power BI / Case, queue, decision and outcome data for reporting / Out / Daily batch / Workbench / Nightly' and 'INT-20 / COLLINS / Decisions and outcomes for model learning / Out / Daily batch to the data lake / Workbench / Nightly'. Architecture v5 slide 37: 'Interface Specifications v3: INT-19/20 (data lake, Power BI) are removed'. Architecture v5 slide 8 notes: 'No data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed)'. Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-13 and JOB-15. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting; none; gap if the story needs lake data'.
Proposed fix: Agree the reporting output path with the reporting owner and the business: either a REST or file interface from rwb-reporting to the bank reporting layer and Power BI, or a second Kafka consumer outside the 19 services, and give it the next free interface ID. Agree separately whether COLLINS model learning is served from the decision records on rwb.decision-record.v1 and by whom.

Title: No PII topic, schema or sender library is named for INT-22, the audit and PII path
Detail: Version 3 gives INT-22 the direction Out, the owner the ACE team, the standard AsyncAPI 3.0 and the payload 'Who, what, when, which record, which fields', sent as events happen, with the ACE logging service setting the retry. Architecture v5 slide 30 (2) says every service sends audit and personal-data access logs through ACE's PII Kafka path to the SOC, and slide 23 says Recovery gets its own business-event topics, separate from ACE's PII logging topics. Neither source names the PII topic, its message schema, the library that writes it or the alert when the SOC path is down, so no service can implement the interface from the documents.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-22: 'PII Kafka, audit and SOC logs / Personal data access, audit and security events / Out / ACE logging / ACE team / Each event / Who, what, when, which record, which fields / As they happen / ... / As the ACE logging service / As the ACE logging service / ACE team / AsyncAPI 3.0 / None'. Architecture v5 slide 30 (2): 'every service sends audit and personal-data access logs through ACE's PII Kafka path to the SOC'. Architecture v5 slide 23: 'Recovery gets its own business-event topics and access rules, separate from ACE's PII logging topics'.
Proposed fix: Obtain the PII topic name, the message schema, the client library and the delivery guarantee from the ACE team and record them against INT-22, and state in the observability story that the library is used and not written by each service.

Title: Environment names for per-service deployment
Detail: Version 4 names four environments (DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD) for one service and leaves one environment token unresolved: the parameter temporal.target reads rwb-temporal-frontend.{env}.svc.cluster.local:7233. Architecture v5 turns that service into 19 services, each with an API deployment and a worker deployment in each environment, but no source gives the name a service or its two deployments take inside an environment: the Helm release name, the Kubernetes deployment names and the DNS name. No source says either whether the token {env} resolves to one value per environment or to a different value for each service and environment. Version 5 keeps the four environment names, keeps {env} character for character, and adds no per-service name.
Evidence: Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 2: 'DEV / Build and developer testing / Synthetic only / On every merge into main / Squads' and the other three rows. Section 3 Temporal server row: 'Official Temporal Helm chart, Helm release rwb-temporal in the ACE namespace, one cluster per environment on the ACE AKS clusters'. Section 6.1: 'temporal.target / rwb-temporal-frontend.{env}.svc.cluster.local:7233 / Temporal worker and WorkflowGateway'. Architecture v5 slide 8: 'RECOVERY · 19 SERVICES · namespace rwb-recovery' and slide 8 notes: '19 services in the rwb-recovery namespace, each an api and a worker deployment'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes: 'an API deployment (2 pods for availability, scaled on CPU or requests if ever needed) and a worker deployment scaled by KEDA'. Ownership Map v1, sheet Services, columns Code, Service, Name, Wave, Schema, REST base, Topic, Queue.
Proposed fix: Fix one naming convention with SCB IT and the ACE platform team: a Helm release per service, a deployment name for the API part and one for the worker part, a service DNS name, and the value of {env} for each of DEV, SIT, UAT and PROD. Record the convention in this document and in the service template specification, and apply it to the 19 services before the wave 1 infrastructure story is accepted.

Title: Kubernetes namespace of the 19 services against the namespace of the Temporal release
Detail: Version 4 puts the single recovery service in the ACE namespace and installs the Temporal chart as Helm release rwb-temporal in the ACE namespace. Architecture v5 draws the 19 services in a Kubernetes namespace named rwb-recovery, and the Temporal and Drools design repeats that placement. The two sources do not settle whether the Recovery services leave the ACE namespace, whether rwb-recovery is the only new namespace, or whether the Temporal release stays in the ACE namespace next to the services it serves. Version 5 places the 19 services in rwb-recovery and keeps the Temporal release in the ACE namespace exactly as version 4 records it, and raises the placement as a gap.
Evidence: Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 1: 'The ACE service on the shared ACE AKS clusters'. Section 3 Service row: 'The ACE Spring Boot service with the recovery module, in the ACE namespace'. Section 3 Temporal server row: 'Helm release rwb-temporal in the ACE namespace'. Architecture v5 slide 8: 'ACE AKS CLUSTER · SHARED' with 'RECOVERY · 19 SERVICES · namespace rwb-recovery'. Architecture v5 slide 8 notes: '19 services in the rwb-recovery namespace'. Temporal and Drools design slide 20 notes: 'Production: official Helm chart on ACE AKS with mTLS (README), Temporal 1.30+'. Neither source states the namespace of the Temporal release under the 19-service split.
Proposed fix: Agree the namespace layout with the ACE platform team: one rwb-recovery namespace for the 19 services and their deployments, and either the same namespace or a platform namespace for the rwb-temporal Helm release. Record the choice in this document, in the service template and in the Helm chart values of the release.

Title: Temporal server is pinned at 1.28.1 but Nexus and Worker Versioning need 1.30 or later
Detail: Version 4 records Temporal server 1.28.1 and Temporal Java SDK 1.31.0 as the versions SCB IT approved, and every version change as a platform change under the release process. Architecture v5 and the Temporal and Drools design both require 1.30 or later, because Nexus and Worker Versioning do not exist in 1.28.1, and Architecture v5 lists the upgrade from 1.28.1 as a Wave 0 action. No source states which version is approved for the target, so version 5 keeps 1.28.1 as recorded and states that the two features are not used in the Epic 1 and Epic 2 scope. A decision is needed before a workflow uses Nexus, which includes the restructure calculator call into ace-collection, or before Worker Versioning is required for a release.
Evidence: Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 3 Temporal server row: 'Server and Java SDK versions are pinned to the SCB IT approved release: Temporal server 1.28.1 and Temporal Java SDK 1.31.0'. Section 3.1: 'a change of either version is a platform change under the release process'. Architecture v5 slide 23 note: 'Upgrade from 1.28.1 to 1.30 or later for Nexus and Worker Versioning'. Architecture v5 slide 31 risks: 'Temporal upgrade from 1.28.1 / No Nexus, no Worker Versioning / Upgrade to 1.30+ in Wave 0'. Temporal and Drools design slide 1 and slide 20 notes: 'Version 1.30+ for Nexus and Worker Versioning' and 'Temporal 1.30+'. Risks and Assumptions v4 row R-18 keeps the version approval open.
Proposed fix: Submit the version list for approval again and pin the approved 1.30 or later server and its matching Java SDK in Wave 0, with the upgrade tested in SIT as a one-minor-version upgrade. Until the approval lands, keep 1.28.1 and keep every Nexus call, including the restructure calculator, out of the scope of a release.

Title: The 19 database logins and the per-service connection budget are not named
Detail: Version 4 names two database roles only: recovery_svc, the single recovery service login, and ace_view_owner, the NOLOGIN role that owns the views. Architecture v5 requires 19 schemas and 19 logins on the ACE PostgreSQL server with a connection budget per service and no cross-schema access, and asks the ACE team and the DBA for it. No source gives the login names, the naming rule for them, the size of a connection pool per service or the total connection budget, so version 5 keeps recovery_svc as the login of rwb-source-data, because the ACE Source Views v1 grants name that role, and leaves the other 18 logins and every pool size unset.
Evidence: Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 3 ACE read role row: 'recovery_svc, the recovery service role: SELECT on recovery.v_ace_* only, no direct public read, no write. ace_view_owner: a NOLOGIN ACE role'. Section 3 Temporal persistence row: 'owned by temporal_svc'. Architecture v5 slide 8: '19 Recovery schemas, one login and connection pool each'. Architecture v5 slide 39 decision 2: '19 schemas and 19 logins on the ACE PostgreSQL server; connection budget per service; no cross-schema access / Owner: ACE team, DBA'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes: 'The ACE database sees capped pools per service.'
Proposed fix: Have the DBA fix the login name per schema, the pool size per service and the total connection budget, and add them to this document and to the ACE DB story of each service. Keep recovery_svc as the name of the rwb-source-data login so that the ACE Source Views v1 grants stay valid, and state the rule for the other 18 names.

Title: The shared Quartz tables are either kept by Epic 1 and Epic 2 or no longer used
Detail: Version 4 keeps Quartz for the Epic 1 and Epic 2 scheduled jobs, keeps Spring Batch for their automated chains, and states that the Workbench adds no qrtz_ or batch tables and shares ACE's existing Quartz and Spring Batch tables. Architecture v5 says that the ACE shared Quartz and batch tables are no longer used by Recovery, because every job becomes a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service, while the decision log and the ADR keep Quartz and the TimerScheduler port for Epic 1 and Epic 2 and the Ownership Map keeps JOB-05 as a timer check behind that port with no Temporal Schedule. The two positions can both be true only if the Epic 1 and Epic 2 jobs stay on the shared tables until their delta stories move them, and no source states that cut-over point. Version 5 keeps the built behaviour and states that the new services add no qrtz_ or batch tables.
Evidence: Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 3 Scheduler row: 'Quartz for Epic 1 and Epic 2 scheduled jobs, and Spring Batch for their automated chains ... JOB-05 timer check runs on Quartz behind the TimerScheduler port ... The Workbench adds no qrtz_ or batch tables and shares ACE's existing Quartz and Spring Batch tables'. Architecture v5 slide 44: 'No shared Quartz tables: a Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow in the owning service; bank Airflow triggers the edges'. Architecture v5 slide 44 notes: 'The ACE shared Quartz and batch tables are no longer used by Recovery.' Decision Log v10 D-RCV-36 T2 and ADR-011 keep Quartz and the TimerScheduler port for Epic 1 and Epic 2. Ownership Map v1, sheet Jobs, JOB-05.
Proposed fix: State the cut-over in the scheduling design: which Epic 1 and Epic 2 jobs stay on the shared Quartz and Spring Batch tables, on which release they move to a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow, and who runs the shared tables once Recovery stops using them. Keep the TimerScheduler port until the JOB-05 delta story is accepted.

Title: Retry-topic and dead-letter topic names are not specified
Detail: Version 3 has no Kafka retry or dead-letter rule, and Arch v5 describes the ladder as the retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and then the .dlt topic. No source in this WP gives the topic names, partitions or the exact suffix set of the retry topics and the .dlt topic for rwb.<short>.events.v1, so the standard states the ladder and the owner and leaves the names open.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 ('Retry topics 1 min / 10 min / 1 h, then .dlt + alert') and slide 22 ('Failures go to retry topics (1 min, 10 min, 1 h) and then to the dead-letter topic'); Template and Rules v1 §R4 ('topic rwb.<short>.events.v1, with retry and .dlt topics'); no naming rule for retry or .dlt topics in the WP sources
Proposed fix: Name the topics rwb.<short>.events.v1.retry.1m, rwb.<short>.events.v1.retry.10m, rwb.<short>.events.v1.retry.1h and rwb.<short>.events.v1.dlt in the naming library (RWB-PLT-E1047) and the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog, and cite them from section 8.3 of this standard.

Title: The source sends report queries to the data lake copy, and the target architecture removes the data lake
Detail: Version 2 scaling bullet 2 says that read queries for reports go to the data lake copy and not to the live database. Architecture v5 removes the data lake and gives rwb-reporting (P9) a read model built from the events, and DP-17 retires the lake paths. The source has no statement of where a report query goes once the lake is gone, and the bullet cannot be kept as written without contradicting the target architecture.
