Evidence: v2 section 3 bullet 2 ('read queries for reports go to the data lake copy, not the live database'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 (no data lake) and slide 41 (P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard, regulatory reports); Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17 ('Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 - Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting'); JOB-15 owner P9 (regulatory extract, no data lake).
Proposed fix: The bullet is rewritten to the rwb-reporting read model built from the events (ADR-018), and the sentence keeps its two prohibitions: not the 19 live schemas, and not a data lake.

Title: The case match of an intake item has no consumed contract in Architecture v5
Detail: Section 2 says the intake agent matches the document to the case by case number, account or name, and section 6 scopes a read to the case, so rwb-document needs the case identity and the case scope of the caller. Architecture v5 slide 16 lists no rwb-case REST operation among the IN contracts of rwb-document, and the Ownership Map has no consumed-operation row for P5 against P3. The design therefore needs a stated reading of how the case is reached.
Evidence: Source section 2 bullet 4 and section 6 bullet 2; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 IN line ('POST /documents, GET /documents/{id}, /cases/{id}/documents, POST /documents/generate; AgentRunCompleted; DocumentIntakeWorkflow'); Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: no P3 operation with consumer P5.
Proposed fix: Read the case identity and the case scope through the case contract of P3 rwb-case over REST (one hop, 2 s timeout) with a contract fake, class C, and record it as a consumed contract of P5.

Title: The legal hold is a case operation in the Ownership Map and a hub rule in the source design
Detail: The source makes a legal hold on a case or document stop expiry, and places the retention class and the hold together in the document hub. The Ownership Map gives POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold to P3 rwb-case and gives rwb_document no legal-hold table, while Architecture v5 slide 16 lists retention under P5. The document therefore has to say where the hold is recorded and how rwb-document learns of it.
Evidence: Source section 7 bullet 2; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet row 'POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold' with owner P3; Tables sheet rows for P5: no legal_hold table; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 OUT line ('metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, signatures, retention').
Proposed fix: Record the hold in rwb-case (P3), have rwb-document read it before an expiry is proposed, and keep retention_rule and retention_action in rwb_document.

Title: O05, decisions and outcomes for model learning, has no path once the data lake is removed
Detail: O05 sends decisions and outcomes to COLLINS daily through the data lake for model learning, and slide 2 sends the same batch to Power BI and COLLINS. Architecture v5 removes the data lake (INT-19 and INT-20, ADR-018, DP-17) and gives rwb-reporting a read model built from events. O04, reporting, has that replacement in P9; O05, model learning, does not: no source names a service, an interface or a file that carries decisions and outcomes to COLLINS after the lake is removed.
Evidence: Information Flow v5 slide 6: 'O05 / Decisions and outcomes for model learning / COLLINS / Daily batch to the data lake / Daily'; slide 2: 'Power BI and COLLINS: daily batch to the data lake'. Architecture v5 slide 37: 'Data lake and Power BI feed (INT-19/20) / Removed: reports from rwb-reporting'; slide 8: 'Data lake / Power BI - not connected (INT-19/20 removed)'. Rules R5.5 DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting / none; gap if the story needs lake data'.
Proposed fix: Confirm with the model owner whether COLLINS needs decisions and outcomes at all after wave 1. If it does, name the path (P9 rwb-reporting read model, or an outbound file through P2 rwb-integration) and add the story; until then O05 is out of scope and the deck says so.

Title: The data lake row and INT-19 and INT-20 are kept while Architecture v5 removes them
Detail: Version 3 keeps the system 'Data lake and Power BI' with disposition 'Keep and feed' and the interfaces INT-19 (case, queue, decision and outcome data for reporting, out, file, daily) and INT-20 (decisions and outcomes to COLLINS for model learning, out, daily batch to the data lake), both owned by the Workbench. Architecture v5 removes the data lake: slide 2 notes 'Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19/INT-20 are removed', slide 7 says 'No data lake or Power BI connection (INT-19/20 removed)', slide 9 says the data lake and Power BI are not connected, and slide 37 lists the data lake and Power BI feed among the parts that go. DP-17 and ADR-018 replace the feed with a read model in rwb-reporting built from events and call for a gap where a story needs lake data. This work package keeps every section, ID and row of the source, so the three rows stay with their v3 wording and carry P9 rwb-reporting as the owning service; the build story for them is not raised.
Evidence: v3 sheet Disposition: 'Data lake and Power BI / Bank reporting / Keep and feed / Not applicable / Workbench / Receives case, queue, decision and outcome data daily / E1 / INT-19 / None'. v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-19 / Data lake and Power BI / ... / Out / File / Daily batch / Daily / DP03, DP12 / Not applicable / Workbench / E1 / File specification / None' and 'INT-20 / COLLINS / ... / Out / File / Daily batch to the data lake / Daily / DP12 / Not applicable / Workbench / E2 / File specification / None'. Architecture v5 slide 2 note, slide 7, slide 9 and slide 37. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17: 'Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting; none; gap if the story needs lake data'.
Proposed fix: Keep the three rows in this inventory and record them as removed from build. If the business needs a reporting output, raise it as a new interface with a free ID against rwb-reporting when the reporting read model is specified; serve model learning from the decision records on rwb.decision-record.v1 (P7) if it is still needed, as the Temporal and Drools design describes.

Title: The data product of INT-06 (AAL) reads To confirm
Detail: INT-06 carries the data product 'To confirm' where every other interface names a DP number or 'None'. The row is the AAL feed, 'Data ACE already receives through COLLINS', and the disposition row for AAL says ACE ingests the data through COLLINS and the Workbench reads it through the account and customer views. The value is the marker of a missing answer and not a data product, so it is kept character for character and no DP number is assigned in this version.
Evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-06 / AAL / Data ACE already receives through COLLINS / In / COLLINS / ACE ingests the COLLINS batch / Daily, end of day / To confirm / Yes / ACE team / E1 / File specification / DL12'. v3 sheet Disposition row AAL: 'Data ACE already receives / Keep / Yes / ACE team / ACE ingests the data through COLLINS and the Workbench reads it through the account and customer views'.
Proposed fix: Name the data product of INT-06 from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the data product catalogue at the next revision of the interface specifications.

Title: The plan names no test ID and no per-service test
Detail: The plan has 8 whole-system tests, no test identifier and no row that can be attached to one of the 19 services or to one journey. The realignment needs a per-service and a journey NFR test, and there is no source ID to inherit.
Evidence: Section 1 table columns are Test, How, Pass mark and When only; the 8 rows are whole-system tests (Load, Stress, Volume, Batch window, Resilience, Restore, Security, Accessibility); no service, epic or journey is named anywhere in the document.
Proposed fix: New IDs NFT-<service code>-01 to -05, NFT-J-01 to -12 and NFT-PLT-01 to -08 are allocated under D-RCV-60; sections 6 to 8 carry the rows and section 5 states the convention.

Title: The source does not say how the data in a fake relates to the sandbox seed
Detail: Version 3 seeds one data set and reads source data through views. With 19 services, a consumer test uses a fake instead of the provider, so the two sides must agree on the business keys. No source states whether a fake carries its own data, a copy of the seed or the same key set.
Evidence: Version 3 section 2: the sandbox is the only test data set below SIT. Template and Rules v1 R5.4: class C, build against the published contract and its fake. Architecture v5 slide 11: contract tests run in every build.
Proposed fix: One key set (caseId, accountId, partyKey) is shared by the seed and every fake; each fake is loaded from the seed file of its provider and reloaded when the seed changes, so no second data set exists.

Title: The definition of ready does not require a published contract
Detail: Version 3 asks the story to state the trigger, the service, the events published, the idempotency key and any call out of the module, and it does not require the contract to be published, versioned or faked before the story is pulled. Version 4 keeps item 8 and adds section 2.3, items 21 to 25: contract published in the Service Contract Catalog v1, fake published, version fixed, ownership stated, Ready to start.
Evidence: Section 2.1 item 8, one cell of text, naming no contract document, no version and no fake. Architecture v5 slide 11: every service publishes its contracts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, activity jar) before code; contract tests run in every build. Template and Rules R5.4: a class C dependency builds against the published contract and its fake.
Proposed fix: Confirm the five items of section 2.3 as mandatory for every story that consumes or provides a contract, and confirm the Service Contract Catalog v1 as the place the contract is published.

Title: The definition of done names no boundary test and no contract test result
Detail: Version 3 lists contract tests inside the nine pipeline gates and requires the story to touch one module, and it never makes a boundary test a result of its own nor says what the boundary is once the monolith is split. Version 4 keeps both items, reads one module as one service and one schema, and adds section 3.5, items 21 to 27: contract tests green, boundary test green, event compatibility, replay test, decision record test, version published, fake retired.
Evidence: Section 3.1 item 2: build and unit tests, lint, secret scan, PDPA lint, container scan, module boundary, integration and contract tests, AI first-pass review and human approval. Section 3.2 item 12: the story touches one module, or the other module's code owner has approved. Architecture v5 slide 29: boundary test fails on a cross-schema reference. Architecture v5 slide 46: contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests, Testcontainers.
Proposed fix: Confirm the seven items of section 3.5 as the results that decide Done, and confirm that the module boundary gate of item 2 is the same gate as the boundary test.

Title: One module means the monolith module in the source and a service and schema after the split
Detail: Two source rows use module as the unit a plan and a story may touch: the plan touches one module, and the story touches one module or the other module's code owner approves. After D-RCV-60 the unit is the service and its schema rwb_<short>, and the owner is the team of the Ownership Map v1. Version 4 reads module as service and schema and keeps the wording of both rows otherwise unchanged.
Evidence: Section 1 row Plan approved: the plan names every file, test and migration and touches one module. Section 3.2 item 12: the story touches one module, or the other module's code owner has approved. Architecture v5 slide 29: one schema per service, no cross-schema joins or keys, a boundary test in every build. Ownership Map v1: 19 services and 19 schemas.
Proposed fix: Confirm that one module is read as one service and its schema from this version on.

Title: The document family has no source file, so no version, section, ID or date can be carried forward
Detail: The work package names the Recovery Workbench Integration Test Plan as an output but the folder holds no file of this family in any version, and no other folder of the document set holds one. A plan written against a missing source keeps no section, identifier, number or date, and its version sequence starts at 1.
Evidence: Folder 09 Testing and quality holds the Test Strategy, Non Functional Test Plan, Test Data Plan, Definition of Ready and Done, Defect Management Process, User Acceptance Test Plan, Test Cases, Regression Suite and Requirements Traceability Matrix, and no Integration Test Plan in any version; a recursive search for a file name containing Integration Test returns no result.
Proposed fix: Issue version 1 with date 22 November 2026, a Supersedes row reading None (first version), and a change-log row that states the family is new; no predecessor section, ID, number or date is cited.

Title: No source states an integration-level exit threshold
Detail: The test strategy fixes the exit of the SIT, UAT and Release gates and of the four wave gates as every journey of the wave passing with no open severity 1 or 2 defect. It states no pass rate, no percentage and no defect density for the integration level, and no other source read for this plan supplies one.
Evidence: Test strategy version 3 section 3 exit column: 'Every wave 1 journey passes; no open severity 1 or 2'; section 7: 'A release goes with no open severity 1 or 2 defect'. No integration pass rate appears in the test strategy, the non-functional test plan version 3, Template and Rules section R5 or the ITG stories.
Proposed fix: Adopt the SIT exit wording of the test strategy version 3 for every wave gate and invent no pass rate; a gate closes on every journey test case passing with no open severity 1 or 2 defect.

Title: The number and calendar of integration test cycles per wave are not stated
Detail: A wave gate is defined by its entry and its exit and by no date. No source read for this plan states how many integration cycles a wave runs, how long a cycle takes or when it starts relative to the wave release date, so the plan cannot state a test window.
Evidence: Test strategy version 3 section 3 gives the wave gates entry and exit conditions only; Template and Rules section R5.6 gives a wave per business epic and no calendar; the ITG journey stories name a business date as test data and no test window.
Proposed fix: Fix one integration test cycle per wave that closes the wave gate before the first release date of the wave, assert no window beyond that, and keep every release date unchanged and tentative.

Title: How SIT is composed while a later-wave service is not deployed is not stated
Detail: The target arrives in four waves, so a wave run in SIT meets services that exist and services that do not. The test strategy says the statement of how SIT is composed across waves is not in any source, and no other source read for this plan fills the gap, so the plan cannot say whether a later-wave contract is faked, stubbed or omitted in a wave journey.
Evidence: Test strategy version 3 section 2: 'the statement of how SIT is composed across waves is not in any source read for this document'; Template and Rules section R5.4 allows a C dependency to be built against a published contract and its fake, and says nothing about the composition of a shared environment.
Proposed fix: Serve every contract of a service that is not yet deployed by its published fake, name every stubbed hop in the journey report, and never count a stubbed hop as a real-owner pass.

Title: Which non-functional requirements are proven at the integration level is not stated
Detail: The non-functional specification gives 78 requirements with a target and a test method each, and the non-functional test plan version 3 schedules them per service, per journey and per platform area. Neither states which identifiers a wave gate reads as integration evidence and which stay at the system level, so a reader of this plan cannot tell how far the integration gate reaches.
Evidence: Non-functional specification v3 requirement rows carry an ID, a target, an owner and a status and no test level; non-functional test plan version 3 sections 6 to 8 hold NFT-<service>-<nn>, NFT-J-<nn> and NFT-PLT-<nn> rows with a when column and no level.
Proposed fix: Read the integration evidence as the two RWB-ITG-NFR stories, the NFT-J rows and the NFR level test cases of the wave journeys, and leave every other identifier to the per-service and system tests of the non-functional test plan.

Title: Name, version and location of a contract fake
Detail: A story with a class C dependency builds against the other service's published contract and its fake, and section 12.8 of the story has to list that fake. No source document gives the fake a name, a version scheme or a place to publish it, so a Given line can only say 'the <service> contract fake'.
Evidence: Section R5.5 DP-11 reads 'REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout'; section R7.2 section 12.8 names the table 'Contract fakes' but not the artefact; the Arch v5 text extract and the Service Contract Catalog v1 carry contracts, not fakes.

Title: The autonomy levels let an agent act, while the architecture says AI only suggests and a person approves

Proposed fix: Confirm that the exception queue of v4 is the dead-letter topic of the target, that the owner named by the rule is the producing service, and that the alert and the replay tool are the recovery path.

The derivation of the idempotency key is therefore unstated, and the outbox and inbox of the target need one rule.
Evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Rules row Duplicates: 'Each event carries an event ID and an idempotency key; a repeat is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40)'. Architecture v5 slide 22: 'Each records ce_id in its inbox table (processed_event) in the same transaction as its own change'. No source derives a separate idempotency key.
Proposed fix: Confirm that the idempotency key of an event is its ce_id, that the inbox table processed_event holds ce_id as its key, and that the duplicate count of R-UNI-40 is taken from the inbox.

Title: The repository name and location for a service are not fixed by any source
Detail: The sources state that each service has one repository and that Wave 0 builds the template and the repositories, but neither the repository naming convention nor the location is given. The Service Template Specification states the layout inside the repository and carries the §R9 placeholder for its name and location.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 38: 'Service template + Helm'. TSD T1: 'one service, one repository, one front end'. No repository name appears in the read set.
Proposed fix: Set the repository naming convention and location in Wave 0 and record them in the Engineering Practices.

Title: The Helm chart name, the release naming and the container registry are not fixed
Detail: Architecture v5 states one Helm chart for all services, an API deployment and a worker deployment per service, and about 38 small deployments at rest. It does not name the chart, the release pattern or the container registry. The Service Template Specification and the Service Catalog carry the §R9 placeholder for these names.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 33: 'one Helm chart and one pipeline template'. Slide 38: 'Service template + Helm'. No chart, release or registry name appears in the read set.
Proposed fix: Name the chart, the release pattern and the registry in Wave 0 and record them in the Environment and Deployment Design.

Title: The event catalogue does not name the consumers of ApprovalDecided or ReportPublished
Detail: ApprovalDecided (rwb.decision.events.v1) and ReportPublished (rwb.reporting.events.v1) appear in the OUT lines of P7 and P9, but neither appears in the event catalogue rows 01 to 30 or in the '+' rows, so no consumer is named. The Service Catalog and its Events published sheet carry the §R9 placeholder for both.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14: P7 OUT 'topic rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce'. Slide 15: P9 OUT 'rwb.reporting.events.v1: ReportPublished'. Slides 42 and 43 list neither event.
Proposed fix: Name the consumer of ApprovalDecided and of ReportPublished in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog v1.

Title: The pipeline tool and its stage names are not fixed by any source
Detail: The sources state one golden pipeline template that every service includes, and that each service runs its own Flyway migrations in its own pipeline. They do not name the pipeline tool or its stages. The Service Template Specification carries the §R9 placeholder.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 33: 'one Helm chart and one pipeline template'. Slide 38: 'golden pipeline'. Slide 29: 'Flyway per service, in its own pipeline'. No tool name appears in the read set.
Proposed fix: Name the pipeline tool and the golden pipeline stages in Wave 0 and record them in the Engineering Practices.

Title: No earlier Service Catalog or Service Template Specification exists in the document set
Detail: Both documents are new at v1. There is no earlier version from which to carry section numbers, IDs, numbers or dates, and no approval status to inherit. The new documents are issued as version 1 with status Draft, and the first change log row is the D-RCV-60 row.
Evidence: Folder 05 Technical architecture holds no Service Catalog or Service Template Specification. Template and Rules §R8.4 names both as v1 outputs of this run.
Proposed fix: Accept version 1 as the baseline and carry it into the Change Register; no earlier identifiers exist to preserve.

Title: DailyCaseRun is described both as a Schedule and as an event-started workflow
Detail: Architecture v5 slide 14 writes 'DailyCaseRun (Schedule + AceDataReady)' and slide 44 writes 'AceDataReady -> DailyCaseRun' for the same job. The two readings differ for build: a Schedule needs a cron, an overlap policy and a catch-up window, and an event-started workflow needs an event contract and an idempotency key. The design lists the job as event-started and records the Schedule as a fallback that is not configured in the target.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 TMP cell: 'CaseWorkflow (parent, one per case) - DailyCaseRun (Schedule + AceDataReady) - Act: allocate, transfer, rebalance'. Slide 44 row JOB-02: 'Airflow: ACE data ready / rwb-case / AceDataReady -> DailyCaseRun'. Slide 31 notes make AceDataReady the trigger of the morning run.
Proposed fix: Confirm that DailyCaseRun is started by AceDataReady only in the target, and that the Schedule named on slide 14 is a fallback for a day when Airflow does not signal the business date.

Title: The rwb-platform task queue has no service definition
Detail: JOB-21 the stuck workflow scan and JOB-22 the platform smoke run on task queue rwb-platform. rwb-platform is not one of the 19 service queues of the Ownership Map Services sheet, and no source says which deployment hosts the platform worker, whether that worker has a schema of its own in the ACE database, what its queue name is in a lower environment, or how its task queue is rate-limited. The ownership of both jobs is given as platform (PLT) with no service code.
Evidence: Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-22 reads 'Starts PlatformSmokeWorkflow as platform-smoke-{yyyymmdd} on task queue rwb-platform through WorkflowGateway'. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives owner 'platform' for JOB-21 and JOB-22. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services lists 19 rows, P1 to P10 and S1 to S9, and none is rwb-platform.
Proposed fix: Define the platform worker: the deployment that hosts it, the task queue name per environment, its schema or its lack of one, and the quotas of the rwb-platform queue.

Title: The case workflow ID is written two ways
Detail: Temporal and Drools design slide 13 says the CaseWorkflow workflow ID is the case ID and adds that ADR-011 writes it as case-{caseId}. The two forms behave differently: signalWithStart creates a second run if the ID does not match, and the JOB-21 visibility query filters on workflow IDs and search attributes. The catalog does not choose one in the workflow row and records the case ID of the v5 design, with this row as the decision point.
Evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 13 note: 'CaseWorkflow (workflow ID = case ID; ADR-011 writes it as case-{caseId})'. Slide 30 note: 'the CaseWorkflow (ID = case ID) starts on queue rwb-case'. ADR-011 is named as the source of the other form.
Proposed fix: Confirm one workflow ID form for CaseWorkflow and apply it to the case router's signalWithStart, to the child workflow IDs of the stage workflows and to the JOB-21 visibility query.

Title: The Feature List keys every feature on one of 19 modules, and 13 of the module names differ from the Arch v5 service names
Detail: The workbook organises all 378 features by a two-letter module code (P1 to P10 and S1 to S9) and a module name of its own; it has no service column and no service-epic column. Architecture v5 says recovery-core is split into 19 services, one per business module, and the Ownership Map names each one with a code, a short name, a schema, a wave and an epic. The code maps one to one, but 13 module names differ from the service names: P1 Recovery data engine, P4 Access and administration, P5 Document hub, P7 Decision center and log, P8 Payments and posting, P10 Agent runtime, S2 TDR settlement and deed in lieu, S3 Guarantees and guarantors, S4 Litigation and enforcement, S5 Assets and auction, S7 Write-off and recovery, S8 Deviation handling and S9 Partner management. Six are the same: P2, P3, P6, P9, S1 and S6. Nothing in the source says which of the two names is authoritative, and nothing in the source gives a service epic for a feature.
Evidence: Features row 4 has 14 columns and no Service column; By module row 4 has 7 columns and no Service column. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 18: 'recovery-core is split further into 19 services, one per business module, so each can be repurposed later'. Line 2713: 'one deployable and one schema become 19 services with a schema and login each in the same ACE database'. Ownership Map v1 Services sheet: 19 rows, code, service short name, name, wave, schema, REST base, topic, queue.
Owner role: Business architect and the platform solution architect
Proposed fix: Read the module code as the service code and keep the module names as the workbook's own labels; take Service and Service epic from the Ownership Map, in the form 'P1 rwb-source-data' and 'RWB-SVC-P1'; do not rename a module in v5. A later version that wants one name per service takes the Architecture v5 catalogue as its source and raises the renaming as a documentation change.

Title: The workbook carries no wave column, and for 141 of the 378 features the service wave and the business-epic wave differ
Detail: The Feature List gives the business epic (E1 to E8) of every feature and no wave. Under D-RCV-60 a wave comes from two places: the service wave of Arch v5 and the business-epic wave of W-MAP (E1 wave 1; E2 and E3 wave 2; E4 and E5 wave 3; E6, E7 and E8 wave 4). Seventeen service-and-epic pairs disagree, covering 141 rows: P3 with E2 (26 rows), P7 with E2 (16), P4 with E8 (14), P6 with E2 (13), S5 with E4 (14), S6 with E6 (12), S8 with E7 (10), P8 with E4 (8), P6 with E4 (8), P9 with E2 (5), P10 with E2 (4), P10 with E8 (3), P9 with E8 (2), P5 with E2 (2), P10 with E3 (2), P8 with E6 (1) and P9 with E6 (1). In every one the epic wave is later than the service wave, so the service is available before the feature ships.
Evidence: Features sheet has no wave column (14 columns, listed in row 4). Ownership Map v1 Services sheet wave column: P1 to P7, P9 and P10 wave 1; P8, S2, S5 and S8 wave 2; S1, S3, S4 and S6 wave 3; S7 and S9 wave 4. W-MAP: 'EP01 / 1; EP02, EP03 / 2; EP04, EP05 / 3; EP06, EP07, EP08 / 4'. Counted on the 378 feature rows of the copied sheet.
Owner role: Programme planner and the platform solution architect
Proposed fix: Do not add a wave column in v5. Take the wave at story stage under R5.6: the W-MAP wave of the business epic, and a story whose W-MAP wave is earlier than its service wave keeps the W-MAP wave. The Read me Counts note states the wave of each service so the reader can see both.

Title: Two features govern feature flags in module P3 while the default ruling puts the flag store in the platform library
Detail: FEAT-CWC-26 controls module release with dated feature flags and FEAT-CWC-29 accepts a queue placement that is disabled by feature flag until a consumer exists; both are P3 features. The R3 default ruling gives feature flags to the platform library, and the Ownership Map gives feature_flag and feature_flag_change to PLT with ruling ASM-A6-tables-7, which has rwb-integration serve the admin API against the library. The source treats the flag as part of the case and workflow module and says nothing about where the flag store lives, so the two rows do not say which service holds the flag.
Evidence: FEAT-CWC-26: 'Control module release with dated feature flags', module P3, class Admin, story key C6. FEAT-CWC-29: 'Accept a queue placement from a model or an agent ... Disabled by feature flag until a consumer exists', module P3, story key N9. Template and Rules R3 default ruling table: 'Feature flags / Platform library'. Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: feature_flag and feature_flag_change owner PLT; Rulings sheet: 'Feature flags stay with the platform library (PLT, R-PREC default ruling); P2 serves the admin API against the library'.
Owner role: Platform library lead and the solution architect of P3 rwb-case
Proposed fix: Keep both features in P3 as the administration capability that sets and reads a flag, with the Service column at P3 under the module rule. The flag table, its change history and the admin API are the platform library's (RWB-PLT-LIB), served through the rwb-integration admin API; no change to the workbook.

Title: No rwb-valuation table in the Ownership Map for the route decision
Detail: The Ownership Map lists RouteDecisionWorkflow as S1 rwb-valuation, but the Tables sheet has no owner S1 row (no valuation table and no route-decision table). The Case and Workflow Model v6 needs the S1 tables owned for the RouteDecisionWorkflow row.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 Tables: no owner S1; Workflows and activities: RouteDecisionWorkflow owner S1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41: rwb-valuation owns valuations and the D6 route decision.
Proposed fix: Add the S1 valuation and route-decision tables to the Ownership Map, or confirm that S1 writes only decision_log_entry in P7 and reads valuation_ext in P1.

Title: CCMS collateral has no target service in the Ownership Map
Detail: The v5 Case file sheet records collateral as coming from CCMS. The Ownership Map has no collateral table and no target service for CCMS; the Case and Workflow Model v6 needs the owner of collateral data after the realignment.
Evidence: Case file v5 row 'Collateral / Collateral records / CCMS'; Ownership Map v1 Tables has no collateral table; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 gives no collateral table to any of the 19 services.
Proposed fix: Confirm that CCMS stays an outside system and its data is read through the P1 source-data contract, or name an owning service and table.

Title: The Counts tab is blank and the release column holds values that are not releases
Detail: The Counts tab says it is calculated from the Roles tab, but every cell is blank in v4. Three role classes hold values that are not an E number (No login for PT-LED, Through bank channels for three customer parties, and E4 self-service through bank channels), so a count per release column cannot be computed without a reading rule.
Evidence: Counts tab rows 5 to 9: Bank user, Partner user, Customer party, Non-human actor, Total, with every release cell empty; Roles tab values 'No login', 'Through bank channels', 'E4 self-service through bank channels'.
Proposed fix: The grid is kept exactly as v4 leaves it; the class totals 37, 7, 4 and 6 that the Roles tab note states are confirmed and restated in the Read me sheet; no per-release count is produced until a reading rule is agreed.

Title: No approval and no status is recorded for the document
Detail: The workbook carries a version, a date and a supersession note but no status, document owner or approval. Under D-RCV-60 the next version is therefore issued as Draft and the missing approval is recorded rather than waited for.
Evidence: Roles tab row 2: 'Version 4, 15 November 2026'; Key tab row 'Version / v4 / 15 November 2026. Supersedes v3'; no status, owner or approval cell in any sheet.
Proposed fix: v5 is issued as Draft under D-RCV-60 with the application owner as the approving role; the approval is recorded when the verification loop runs.

Title: Control owner service is not stated in the controls catalog
Detail: The 44 control rows name a performer as a role or a monolith component, for example Rules component, Decision center, Decision log writer, Document hub and ACE access check, and name no service. Version 4 adds one primary owner service per control from the Ownership Map v1, chosen by the table, endpoint, event, workflow or job that the control reads or writes, with the basis in column P. No other cell of a control row changes.
Evidence: Controls column Performed by: 44 rows, each a role, a system or a monolith component; no row names a service. Ownership Map v1 sheets Services, Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities, Jobs and Rulings give the owner per object; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the objects each of the 19 services owns.
Proposed fix: Confirm the owner service of each of the 44 controls with the control owner and the service owner, and keep the owner basis column as the record of the ruling.

Title: Five controls check work that two services own
Detail: Five controls check work held by more than one service: CTL-01 checks the case (P3 rwb-case) and the REC-01 to REC-05 reconciliation (P1 rwb-source-data); CTL-04 checks the approval (P7 rwb-decision) against the DoA limit (P4 rwb-access, delegation_limit); CTL-08 checks the rule package (P7) against reference loads and lists (P3 rwb-case) and DoA limits (P4); CTL-27 checks asset pricing and the re-appraisal schedule (S5 rwb-asset) against the valuation record (S1 rwb-valuation); CTL-31 checks the data tape (S6 rwb-debtsale) against the masking rule (P4). Version 4 records the service that holds the control record as primary owner and names the other owner in the basis column.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41: P3 owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation and timers; P1 owns the ACE view contract, freshness and reconciliation; P7 owns approvals and the central decision ledger; P4 owns roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table and access log; S5 owns assets taken on, holding, floor price and listings; S1 owns valuations; S6 owns lots and the data room. Ownership Map sheets Tables and Endpoints: reconciliation_result P1, approval P7, delegation_limit P4, rule_package P7, parameter_catalog and reference_row P3, listing S5, valuation records S1, masking_rule P4, debt_sale_lot S6.
Proposed fix: Confirm for each of the five controls which service holds the control evidence and which service is tested, so that the control is written once in the test pack and appears against one story.

Title: Control rows still name monolith components and monolith messages
Detail: Rows name the monolith components Rules component, Decision center, Decision log writer, Document hub, ACE access check, Debt sale agent and Write-off agent, and the messages MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-005, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P5-002, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-S4-001, MSG-S2-001, MSG-S2-002 and MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002. Version 4 keeps the wording word for word and records the service in column O, so a row states the realigned owner but still describes the check by its monolith name.
Evidence: Controls column Performed by: Rules component (CTL-01, CTL-03, CTL-21, CTL-22, CTL-25, CTL-34, CTL-35, CTL-42), Decision center (CTL-04, CTL-05, CTL-07, CTL-23, CTL-24, CTL-26, CTL-28), Decision log writer (CTL-06), ACE access check (CTL-09), Document hub (CTL-12, CTL-13), Communications (CTL-14 to CTL-17), Debt sale agent (CTL-31), Write-off agent (CTL-33). Column How it is tested: MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-005, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P5-002, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-S4-001, MSG-S2-001, MSG-S2-002, MSG-S5-001 and MSG-S5-002.
Proposed fix: In the next version, map each monolith component name and each MSG-Px-nnn code to the service and its API or event, keep the old wording in a preserved column, and confirm the mapping with the control owners.

Title: No calendar release date is stated for any control
Detail: First in gives a business epic, E1 to E8, and no date. Version 4 keeps the epics and adds no date, so no release date of a control can be marked tentative. If a date is written into a later version it is tentative (R1 U7), and the programme date set is not stated in the catalog.
Evidence: Controls column First in: E1 10, E2 12, E3 7, E4 2, E5 4, E6 4, E7 3, E8 2; no date cell in any sheet. Template and Rules R1 U7 and R5.6: release dates are tentative and unchanged, and a date is never raised as a gap.
Proposed fix: When the programme date set is published, add the tentative release date beside each epic and mark it (tentative) without changing the epic.

Title: The retention class LAKE_COPY has no target without the data lake
Detail: retention_rule.record_class carries LAKE_COPY for the decision log lake copy. With the data lake removed the class describes no record, while the decision log stays excluded from the monthly job by the table_name rule.
Evidence: Physical Schema v6 comment on retention_rule.record_class: Retention class from LOV-RETENTION, or LAKE_COPY for the decision log lake copy; comment on retention_rule.table_name: never decision_log_entry; Architecture v5 slide 37 and plan DP-17.
Proposed fix: Retire the LAKE_COPY class with the lake and keep the exclusion of decision_log_entry and the JOB-14 hash-chain check.

Title: No source maps a data product to a service schema
Detail: The schedule is per data product, and the target is per schema. The Ownership Map gives a table and an endpoint owner, but no source gives the mapping from DP01 to DP14 to the 19 schemas.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 Tables and Endpoints sheets: table and path owners only; Logical Data Model v8 LOV-DATA-PRODUCT: product codes only; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41: service scope in words.
Proposed fix: Read the mapping from the owner of the tables that carry each data product, and name a record against every schema that holds part of it.

Title: No service owner for any personal data category or control
Detail: The design names roles, tables and paths (contact_point.consent_status, PII Kafka, the partner portal) but never names the service that owns the data or the control in the target architecture.
Evidence: v2 sections 3, 4, 5 and 8 name tables and roles only; Architecture v5 slide 41 and Ownership Map v1 give the owners, so the mapping is a realignment addition, not a source value.
Proposed fix: Assign every owner from Ownership Map v1 and Architecture v5 slide 41; add the per-service boundary table (section 11) and the enforcement table (section 11.2).

Title: PII read log has no event contract
Detail: Every read of a personal field is logged through PII Kafka, but the log event's schema, topic and producer contract are not defined in the sources. The path is the ACE Common PII logging to the SOC, not a business topic.
Evidence: v2 section 5 second bullet; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 34 (audit and PII logging through ACE Common, separate from business topics); no AsyncAPI event for a PII read in the event catalogue on slides 42 and 43.
Proposed fix: Keep the ACE Common PII Kafka path as the only read log; the field-level event contract is delivered by the ACE team and is not created by any Recovery service.

Title: An obligation states no release, wave or date
Detail: Only the controls carry a first release (First in E1 to E8 in the Controls Catalog v4). An obligation has no release, no wave and no date, so the point at which it becomes fully evidenced can only be read from the first release of its controls and the wave of the service that owns them. Version 3 adds no wave column and invents no epic or date: the wave of each service is written inside the basis text of column J, and sheet By service states the wave of each service.
Evidence: Sheet Obligations has eight columns in version 2, none of them a release, epic, wave or date. Template and Rules R5.6 gives the wave per business epic and R1 U7 makes every release date tentative; no date is written in the workbook, so no date is marked (tentative).
Proposed fix: Add a first-in (business epic) column to the obligations once Compliance confirms the scope, and show the wave per obligation in the next version.

Title: The four platform library tables have schema 'platform' in the map but are created in every service schema
Detail: The map gives outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key owner PLT and schema 'platform', while the ruling on the same rows says they are library objects created in every service schema. A single target schema per entity cannot say both, so the column needed a wording of its own.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key (owner PLT, schema platform) with the ruling 'library objects created in every service schema ... ASM-A6-tables-8'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service: own schema with outbox and inbox) and slide 11 (transactional outbox); Template and Rules DP-09.
Proposed fix: Write target schema 'every service schema (platform library object)' for the four rows, keep owner PLT, and record that each service's DB story creates its own copy.

Title: Feature flags are 'Workbench' as system of record in the model but owned by the platform library
Detail: v6 states 'Workbench' as the system of record of both feature-flag tables. The map moves them to the platform library under the default ruling, and P2 only serves the admin API. The preserved column and the new owner now disagree, which is left visible rather than edited.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows feature_flag and feature_flag_change (owner PLT, schema platform) and sheet Rulings row feature_flag (R-PREC default ruling, ASM-A6-tables-7, P2 serves the admin API); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries); v6 Entities rows Feature flag and Feature flag change, System of record 'Workbench'.
Proposed fix: Keep column E word for word, add owner PLT and target schema 'platform library', and note in the next version that P2 serves the admin API against the library.

Title: The Key sheet has no term for the five realignment concepts the new columns use
Detail: The Key defines 16 terms and values of v6: subject area, data product, entity, system of record, the four system-of-record values, the two cardinalities, the two standards and the ACE source view, extension table and business key. It has no term for an owning service, a target schema, the platform library, a cross-service reference or a service contract, which are the words of every new column.
Evidence: v6 Key sheet rows 5 to 21 (16 rows) and row 2 (What each term and value means); v6 has no owning-service column anywhere; Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 (schema, login, topic and package per service) and Ownership Map v1 sheet Services (19 services, 19 schemas).
Proposed fix: Append five Term rows at rows 22 to 26 and leave the 16 v6 rows unchanged.

Title: lake_copy_watermark is still an entity of the inventory although the data lake is removed
Detail: Six fields of lake_copy_watermark are classified as Workbench data. The target architecture has no data lake and no Power BI connection, so the table has nothing to watermark and the inventory still presents it as live data with an on-screen rule and a retention rule.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 67 and line 707 (Recovery has no connection to the data lake; INT-19 and INT-20 removed), line 2988 (JOB-13: the decision log copy is replaced by continuous Kafka ingest); ADR-018; DP-17; Template and Rules R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired).
Proposed fix: The six rows are kept with their field IDs and marked retired with the data lake; the Owner column reads P1 rwb-source-data (retired table) and no copy is built.

Title: Version 5 states one ACE service, one repository, one recovery module and one schema, which Architecture v5 replaces with 19 services
Detail: Version 5 is written for one deployable: one service, one repository, one front end and one recovery module, with module boundaries checked in the build and with modules sharing one PostgreSQL database. Architecture v5 and the realignment cut Recovery into 19 services inside ACE, each with its own repository, schema and login. Architecture v5 wins on source precedence (R3, item 1 over item 9), so version 6 replaces the module boundary with the service and schema boundary and records the loser here.
Evidence: Version 5 section 2.1: 'There is one service, one repository and one front end'; section 1 Structure: 'Modular monolith: common, collection and recovery modules by folder'; section 2.2: 'Each module owns its tables. Another module reads them only through the owning module's interface'; Architecture v5 slide 37 lists 'recovery-core: one deployable (ADR-001)' becoming '19 services, one per BA module' and 'One schema for everything (ADR-002)' becoming 'ACE database, one schema and login per service'; Template and Rules R4 gives 19 services and ADR-013 to ADR-014 record the decision.
Proposed fix: Keep the conflict row closed by D-RCV-60 and retire the module wording at the next review, so that no later document repeats the one service position.

Title: The source carries no change log and no tool line
Detail: Version 5 has a metadata table only and no change log, so there is no record of what changed between version 4 and version 5 and no tool line for the source. Version 6 adds the change-log table, records version 5 as the source row with the gap and the assumption, and gives its own row the D-RCV-60 change and the tool line.
Evidence: The version 5 document ends at section 11 Assumptions and gaps and contains no change-log table, no revision history and no tool line; the converted text of the file has 11 numbered sections.
Proposed fix: Add a change-log table to every later version and reconstruct the rows of versions 4 and 5 from the document properties and the release record.

Title: The Features and Stories counts, and the 'Delivered in' text, are monolith-era and are not restated per service
Detail: The Releases sheet counts 118, 77, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18 and 19 features and 60, 31, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18 and 19 stories by epic, and the Modules by release sheet says when each module is delivered in epic terms ('E1 core, E2 screens'). Both are written for the monolith and its story split. The realignment splits the same legacy work into 1,034 story slices over 358 legacy stories, one service per module, so the plan's counts no longer describe the realigned backlog and the 'Delivered in' text mixes a module with several service releases. No source read gives a per-service or per-wave count, so version 5 keeps every number and every 'Delivered in' text unchanged and records that they are monolith-era counts.
Evidence: Release Plan v4 Releases sheet: Features 118, 77, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18, 19 and Stories 60, 31, 31, 50, 26, 37, 18, 19; split_plan.json stats: slices 1,034, legacy 358, day1 939, lanes 510; Modules by release sheet rows P3 'E1 core, E2 screens' and S2 'E2 foundations; E3'; Template and Rules R5.1 and R5.2 replace the module with the service and the story ID pattern.
Proposed fix: Restate the counts per release from the realigned story set once the Service Story Catalog v1 is assembled, and keep the version 4 numbers as the legacy baseline beside them.

Title: The plan names no owner per release, and no source states which team owns a wave's release readiness
Detail: Version 4 names the roles that receive users and the roles that decide each gate, but no owner per release, per epic or per module. The realignment turns each module into a service with an owner in the Ownership Map v1, and Template and Rules R5.3 gives each work type a suggested team, with no person named anywhere. No source read states who owns a release's readiness across the services of a wave, so version 5 records the service owner codes and the team types as the owner position and leaves the accountable role for a release open.
