Evidence: Target Architecture v6 slide 3 row 'Built on ACE' reads 'The Workbench is a module of ACE: one service, one repository, one front end'; slide 4 principle 2 reads 'One service, one repository, one front end'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes read 'one Helm chart and one pipeline template' as the cost of 19 services and do not name repositories. Rules R5.1 lists 'RWB-PLT-TPL: service template and repositories' with no count.
Proposed fix: State the repository and pipeline model in the service template specification, with the code owners and the boundary test that follow from it.

Title: The Temporal cluster, namespace and workflow kit are owned by a role, not by an owner code
Detail: Layers L1 to L3 of the Temporal layer are owned by 'the platform team': the cluster, the persistence database, the namespaces and the versioned workflow kit. No Ownership Map code owns them: the Map assigns the 15 workflows to service and PLT codes, and the platform jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 to PLT, with no row for the cluster, the namespace rwb-recovery or the kit. Rules R5.1 gives the epics RWB-PLT-WF for the workflow platform and RWB-PLT-LIB for shared libraries, which is the nearest the story plan comes to an owner.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 23 labels L1, L2 and L3 'platform team'; slide 39 decision 3 reads 'Owner: Platform team, ACE team'. Temporal and Drools design slide 12 labels L1 to L3 'platform team'. ownership.json has 15 workflow rows (P3, P5, P6, P7, P10, S1 to S9, PLT) and 22 job rows, of which JOB-05, JOB-11, JOB-21 and JOB-22 are PLT, and no cluster, namespace or kit row.
Proposed fix: Name the PLT epic or story that owns the cluster, the namespace and the workflow kit (RWB-PLT-WF for the platform and RWB-PLT-LIB for the kit in this deck), and record whether the running service is run by the platform team or by ACE.

Title: Eleven business events have no number in the catalogue and three have no contract
Detail: The numbered catalogue stops at 30, and the plus rows (RouteDecided, AssetSold, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled and Settled, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged, FileDelivered and FileFailed) carry no EV number. ReportPublished (P9), LawsuitFiled (S4), ApprovalDecided (P7) and the two split guarantee events (S3) have no AsyncAPI operation.
Evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 plus rows; asyncapi/rwb-reporting.asyncapi.yaml has no channel; asyncapi/rwb-litigation.asyncapi.yaml has no LawsuitFiled; asyncapi/rwb-guarantee.asyncapi.yaml has one GuaranteeClaim message.
Proposed fix: Number the plus rows EV-31 onwards and add the missing operations to the four AsyncAPI documents.

Title: Every module specification is still In review and no approval is recorded
Detail: All 20 source files carry Status In review. D-RCV-60 has no approval round, so the next version is issued as Draft with the status recorded. This is not a defect of the specification; it is the approval state.
Evidence: '/ Status / In review /' in every file of the v5 family.
Proposed fix: Record the approval of the v6 family at the design authority and move Status to Approved.

Title: No squad is named per service
Detail: Every file names 'TechX recovery squads' as the build squad. Under 19 services the squad per service is not specified, and Template and Rules R5.3 keeps the owner a suggestion only.
Evidence: '/ Build squad / TechX recovery squads /' in every file of the v5 family.
Proposed fix: Assign a squad per service at the design authority; the suggestion stays TechX for app work and the ACE team for DB work.

Title: INT-34 (ACE Common) has five consumers and no single owning service
Detail: INT-34 is one published module interface to ACE Common that covers six capabilities, and Architecture v5 slide 30 gives each capability a different consumer: sign-in and access checks to gateway-bff and rwb-access, audit and PII logging to all 19 services, the shared case view to rwb-case, the restructure calculator to rwb-treatment, the notification path to rwb-comms and the shared entities to rwb-source-data. Version 3 gives the row a single owner, the ACE team, and a single owner of the fix, also the ACE team. The realignment needs one Recovery-side owner per interface and no source states which service holds the contract for the whole of INT-34.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-34: 'ACE common module / Shared case view, entities, restructure calculator, notification path / Both / Published module interface / ACE team / Call or application event / As published by the common module / Per request / Per call / Return the error to the calling module / As the caller decides / ACE team / Module interface / DL14'. Architecture v5 slide 30 rows 1 to 6 with the consumer named per capability. Architecture v5 slide 17: 'DB writes schema rwb_integration: interface config, file runs, outbound items, ACE integration paths'. Ownership Map v1, sheet Services: P2 rwb-integration, Integration.
Proposed fix: Agree whether INT-34 stays one interface with rwb-integration as the contract owner and a per-capability client in each consuming service, or splits into one interface row per capability with the consuming service as owner. If it splits, add the new rows in the next version and give each one the capability name of Architecture v5 slide 30.

Title: INT-14 (WIN registered mail) has three different owners in the sources
Detail: Version 3 makes the single Workbench the owner of INT-14 and the owner of the fix an owning team plus the platform administrator. Architecture v5 slide 17 puts the WIN outbound file in rwb-integration, which builds the file and owns the file run, while slide 30 (5) says WIN letters go as a file via rwb-integration and the notice itself is rwb-comms. The Ownership Map ruling for JOB-10 records rwb-comms as the owner of the notice and of the 16:00 window, with rwb-integration performing deliverFile, and the Service Catalog v1 gives the P6 file contract as 'WIN letters handed to rwb-integration (INT-14)'. Two services therefore share the interface and no source names one owner.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-14: 'WIN / Demand, recall and sale notices for registered mail / Out / Batch: outbound file through the integration adapters / Workbench / Notice approved and generated / ... / Owning team, platform administrator'. Architecture v5 slide 17: 'FILE WIN (registered mail): daily outbound file (INT-14)'. Architecture v5 slide 30 (5) note: 'WIN letters go as a file via rwb-integration'. Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings JOB-10: 'rwb-comms (P6) owns the notice and the 16:00 window, and rwb-integration (P2) performs deliverFile as a step'. Service Catalog v1, P6 contract by call type, File row.
Proposed fix: Confirm rwb-comms as the owner of INT-14 (the notice, the addressee and the content of the file) and rwb-integration as the executor of the transfer, and write the split into the P6 and P2 contract stories so that the retry and the acknowledgement have one owner.

Title: INT-25 (debt-buyer data tape) is owned by the Workbench in v3 and by two services in the target
Detail: Version 3 makes the single Workbench the owner of INT-25, the data tape for an awarded lot, and the owner of the fix an owning team plus the platform administrator. Architecture v5 slide 17 puts the debt-buyer encrypted files in rwb-integration, which builds the file and the manifest, while the Service Catalog v1 gives the S6 file contract as 'Buyer file per lot through rwb-integration (INT-25)'. The lot, the accounts and the personal data allowed by the sale terms are rwb-debtsale data. No source names one owner of the interface.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-25: 'Debt buyers / Debt sale data tape for an awarded lot / Out / Batch: outbound file through the integration adapters / Workbench / Lot awarded / BorrCode, OS By Acct, SellingPriceByAcct ... / Owning team, platform administrator'. Architecture v5 slide 17: 'Debt buyers: per lot, encrypted (INT-25)'. Service Catalog v1, S6 contract by call type, File row: 'Buyer file per lot through rwb-integration (INT-25)'.
Proposed fix: Confirm rwb-debtsale as the owner of INT-25 (the lot, the account set and the content of the tape) and rwb-integration as the executor of the encrypted transfer, and write the split into the S6 and P2 contract stories.

Title: INT-24 is screen-based through the external gateway in v3 and gateway-based around rwb-partner in Architecture v5
Detail: Version 3 describes INT-24 as Workbench screens through the external gateway, with the single Workbench as owner, the partner and agency manager as owner of the fix and OpenAPI 3.1 as the standard. Architecture v5 slide 8 says partners use the partner gateway with FAPI 2.0 that fronts rwb-partner, and Architecture v5 slide 30 lists no partner row among the ACE Common capabilities. The integration style therefore differs between the sources, and neither states whether an instruction to a partner is issued as a REST call carrying documents or as a file over the partner gateway.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 row INT-24: 'Partner portal / Instructions to partners and the results they report / Both / Workbench screens through the external gateway / Workbench / Instruction sent or result entered / ... / Show the error to the partner user and keep the entry / The user submits again / Partner and agency manager / OpenAPI 3.1 / DL03'. Architecture v5 slide 8 note: 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'. Architecture v5 slide 8 diagram: 'Partner gateway FAPI 2.0 -> S9'.
Proposed fix: Confirm that INT-24 is the partner gateway interface of rwb-partner (FAPI 2.0, REST, no screen owned by the Workbench beyond the partner portal), that instructions and results travel on it, and whether a file variant exists for firms that cannot use the API.

Title: Field mapping and Key cite Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7 while v8 is the latest in the set
Detail: The Field mapping description says the mappings are per the LDM v7 ACE mapping sheet and the Key row says the field ID is the one of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7. The latest document in the set is v8, and this run produces the next version of the LDM. The field IDs of the format DF-XXX-nnn do not change, so only the citation of the version is out of date; nothing in the mapping changes.
Evidence: Interface Specifications v3 sheet Field mapping row 2: 'per the LDM v7 ACE mapping sheet'. Sheet Key row 'LDM field': 'The field ID in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v7'. _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md is present in the run material.
Proposed fix: Repoint the two citations at the next LDM version when it is issued, and check that every DF-* field ID of the mapping still exists in it; no row of the mapping is expected to change.

Title: Per-service CPU, memory and autoscaling thresholds are not stated
Detail: Version 4 gives no sizing at all, because one service ran on the ACE pattern. Architecture v5 gives the shape of the two deployments, 2 pods for the API part and KEDA scaling of the worker part on the task-queue backlog or consumer lag down to zero, and names the bursty services (document OCR and agent runs), but it gives no CPU or memory request and limit, no KEDA threshold, no maximum replica count and no pod disruption budget for any of the 19 services. Version 5 therefore states the shape and the count of deployments and leaves every figure unset; a worker that can scale to zero and an API part that must keep 2 pods also need a stated minimum and maximum per environment.
Evidence: Environment and Deployment Design v4 section 7: 'Availability / 99.9% in business hours / Proposed, DL11'. Architecture v5 slide 33 notes: 'an API deployment (2 pods for availability, scaled on CPU or requests if ever needed) and a worker deployment scaled by KEDA on the Temporal task-queue backlog or Kafka consumer lag, down to zero for bursty work such as OCR or agent runs'. Architecture v5 slide 4: 'api + worker deployment'. No source gives a request, a limit, a threshold or a replica maximum.
Proposed fix: Set the request and limit, the KEDA threshold and the replica minimum and maximum for the API part and the worker part of each service from the volume forecast, starting with the bursty services rwb-document, rwb-agent, rwb-case and rwb-payment, and record them in the Helm values and in the infrastructure story of each service.

Title: No message ID for a REST hop timeout or a dead-lettered event
Detail: The standard adds no message ID and the error and message standard has no code for a REST hop timeout or for an event parked on a .dlt topic. Version 4 states the RFC 9457 problem detail for the REST timeout and the alert path for the dead letter instead of inventing a code; whether the message standard will add MSG-GEN codes for these two failures is open.
Evidence: Version 3 A43 ('These are the only messages used for the Temporal and Drools failures in this standard. No message ID is added by this standard'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 ('Errors: RFC 9457 problem details', REST column)
Proposed fix: Keep RFC 9457 problem details for a REST hop timeout and the alert path for a .dlt event in this standard, and decide in the error and message standard whether two new MSG-GEN codes are needed.

Title: Role that replays a dead-lettered event is not named
Detail: Arch v5 gives the dead-letter topic an alert and a replay tool but names no role. Version 3 gives the platform administrator the outbound queue and the workflow failures. Version 4 records the platform administrator as the alert and replay role and leaves the split between the platform and the owning service open.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 22 ('then to the dead-letter topic with an alert and a replay tool'); Version 3 A24 (Workflow and Workflow failed rows: 'Platform administrator'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (platform team runs the stuck-workflow scan, JOB-21)
Proposed fix: Record the platform administrator as the role that receives the .dlt alert and runs the replay tool, with the owning service fixing the cause; put the split in the observability and monitoring design.

Title: The 2 s REST timeout equals the 2 s screen target
Detail: Arch v5 gives a 2 s timeout to each REST hop and a 2 s p95 target to the whole screen, planned at about 1.2 s. A hop that runs to its ceiling therefore uses the whole screen budget, and the sources do not say whether the 2 s is a per-call ceiling or the end-to-end budget.
Evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 ('Timeouts 2 s, circuit breaker per downstream, GET retry once with jitter' and 'total about 1.2 s against the 2 s target'); slide 11 ('Timeout, retry: 2 s; retry GET only'); NFR screen response < 2 s (p95)
Proposed fix: Read the 2 s as the per-call ceiling and 1.2 s as the planning figure for the composed screen; record both figures in the availability, performance and recovery design and in the NFR harness.

Title: The source file is v2 in its name and Version 1 in its own table, with the date 28 October 2026
Detail: The file of the family is named v2, and the table at the top of the document says Version 1 and Date 28 October 2026. The family has no change log and no earlier version in the folder, so the two numbers cannot both be the version of the surviving document. The next version has to be named, and the version it continues has to be stated without breaking either number of the source.
Evidence: The source file name 'Recovery Workbench Availability Performance and Recovery Design v2.docx'; its own table rows 'Version / 1' and 'Date / 28 October 2026'; the folder 05 Technical architecture holds no v1 file and no other version of the family; Rules v1 §R8.2 (the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1).
Owner role: Technical documentation with the architecture team
Proposed fix: The file name carries the family version, so the next version is v3 and the change log starts at 3; the source is recorded as 2 as the file name and 1 as the version in its own table, and both numbers are kept in the metadata row 'Source version'.

Title: The nightly copy to the data lake survives in the source and in the v4 batch design
Detail: The source sends a nightly copy of the decision log to the data lake and makes the daily chain check a job. Architecture v5 removes the data lake (INT-19 and INT-20 removed) and replaces the copy with continuous Kafka ingest (JOB-13) and a daily ledger seal to write-once storage (JOB-14 checks the chain). The batch design of the previous version still copies the log to the lake at 01:00.
Evidence: Source section 1 (decision log 'ACE database; nightly copy to the data lake'); Architecture v5 slide 37 ('No data lake'), slide 14 (daily ledger seal, WORM) and slide 44 (JOB-13, JOB-14); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-13 (nightly copy to the data lake, 01:00).
Proposed fix: Remove the data lake copy and its job; keep JOB-13 as the continuous ingest, JOB-14 as the chain check and the daily seal to write-once storage as the archival control. RWB-E1-014 stays retired and its dependencies are dropped.

Title: The source metadata table says Version 1 while the file family is v2
Detail: The document control table of the source states Version 1 and Date 28 October 2026, while the file itself is named 'Document Management Design v2' and no v3 exists in the folder. A next version can only be numbered from the family that the folder holds, so the next version is 3 and the Version 1 statement of the source cannot be carried forward as the version row without contradicting the file name.
Evidence: Source metadata table rows 'Version / 1' and 'Date / 28 October 2026'; file name 'Recovery Workbench Document Management Design v2.docx'; no other file of the family in 05 Technical architecture.
Proposed fix: Number the realigned document 3, keep '1, 28 October 2026' visible in the Source version row and the change log, and align the metadata Version row with the file name at the next review.

Title: e-Discovery is described with no operation in the Ownership Map
Detail: Section 7 requires e-Discovery to return every document for a named population with metadata and versions. The 17 P5 rows of the Endpoints sheet hold no e-discovery operation and no population resource, so the interface that serves the requirement is not specified by any source.
Evidence: Source section 7 bullet 4; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: 17 operations with owner P5, none for e-discovery or a population.
Proposed fix: Serve e-Discovery with GET /documents of rwb-document and the case, type and date filters, returning metadata and the version list; add a dedicated operation only if the legal team needs one.

Title: Document types and checklists are reference data in the source and P5 tables in the Ownership Map
Detail: Section 3 adds further types 'as reference data', and the R-PREC default ruling of Rules v1 R3 gives parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case with the DP-07 reference-data contract. The Ownership Map gives document_type, document_checklist_item and case_document_check to P5 rwb-document. The two readings differ on who owns the type list and through whose contract another service reads it.
Evidence: Source section 3 closing paragraph; Rules v1 R3 default rulings ('Parameters and reference data (E1-042, E1-043): P3 rwb-case', 'Reference data, LOV: rwb-case') and DP-07; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet rows document_type, document_checklist_item, case_document_check with owner P5.
Proposed fix: Keep the document type list and the checklist in rwb_document (P5) and let other services read them through the P5 contract; do not copy them into the rwb-case reference data.

Title: The intake job has no mechanism or frequency in the source design
Detail: Section 2 says the scanner folder is 'picked up by the intake job' and gives no frequency, no owner and no mechanism. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-12 as every 15 minutes, owner rwb-document, mechanism 'event plus KEDA workers', and slide 16 puts OCR, classify and extract in DocumentIntakeWorkflow. The source alone cannot be built from.
Evidence: Source section 2 row 'Branch scanner' and row 'Mailroom'; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-12 row; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 TMP line.
Proposed fix: Run JOB-12 as a 15-minute Temporal trigger that starts DocumentIntakeWorkflow, with KEDA workers scaling on the intake queue.

Title: The search index and the masking rows sit with different owners
Detail: Section 6 says masked fields are not searchable, so the rule has to be applied where the index is built (rwb_document, P5) and where the response is shaped. The masking rows are masking_rule in rwb_access (P4) and the source neither names the table nor says whether the index holds the clear value. No source states which service filters the index.
Evidence: Source section 6 bullets 1 and 4; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet row masking_rule with owner P4 and rows document, document_field with owner P5.
Proposed fix: Index no personal field in clear form, mask every response at the P5 API against the masking_rule rows of rwb-access, and test the index with a national ID search.

Title: E-signature is named in the type table and nowhere else
Detail: The settlement agreement arrives 'generated; e-signature or scan', and Architecture v5 slide 41 lists signatures under P5, with signature_request a P5 table in the Ownership Map. No source gives the request interface, the party model or the result event, and the callers that need a signature (S2 rwb-treatment for a settlement, S6 rwb-debtsale for a lot pack) are not stated in this document.
Evidence: Source section 3 row 'Settlement agreement'; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 OUT line ('signatures'); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet row signature_request with owner P5.
Proposed fix: Record the request in signature_request (P5) and expose it as an activity contract on queue rwb-document, called by the owning service that needs the signature.

Title: The storage is 'Blob storage' in the source and Azure Blob with a WORM container in Architecture v5
Detail: Sections 1 and 2 name 'Blob storage' and a write-once container, with DL27 still open on storage, backup and legal hold. Architecture v5 slide 16 names Azure Blob (WORM) as the file store of P5 and gives the volume (files, 2.8 TB by 2031). The source wording is older and does not name the platform.
Evidence: Source section 1 row 'Storage' and section 2 bullet 2; Architecture v5 slide 16 P5 FILE line ('Azure Blob (WORM): files, 2.8 TB by 2031').
Proposed fix: Name the store as Azure Blob (WORM) with the claim-check pattern and the 2.8 TB by 2031 planning figure, and keep DL27 open for the backup and legal-hold detail.

Title: The overdue-original task has no owner queue
Detail: Section 5 records an overdue original as 'Task to document services; MSG-P5-004 on the case'. Tasks, queues and allocation belong to P3 rwb-case in the Ownership Map, and rwb_document has no task table, so the source sentence does not say which service raises the task or where the officer sees it.
Evidence: Source section 5 row 'Overdue'; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: task and queue resources with owner P3, none with owner P5.
Proposed fix: Raise the task through the task contract of rwb-case (P3), carry MSG-P5-004 on the case, and keep the custody row in rwb_document.

Title: The By route counts are blank in v2 and v3 although the sheet says they are calculated
Detail: The By route sheet carries the line 'Calculated from the Interfaces tab.' and six rows (COLLINS, File, Direct through ACE, Through partners, Not at all today and Total) with four count columns (In, Out, Both, Total), but every count cell is empty in v2 and in v3. The 36 rows of the Interfaces sheet carry the route and the direction of each interface, so the counts can be calculated without adding a value that no source gives. Without them a reader cannot check how many interfaces run in, out or both ways per route, and the statement in the Interfaces description that ACE ingests every inbound source cannot be checked either.
Evidence: v3 sheet By route, row 2: 'Calculated from the Interfaces tab.'; rows 5 to 10: 'COLLINS' with every count cell empty, then 'File', 'Direct through ACE', 'Through partners', 'Not at all today' and 'Total', each with the same four empty cells. v2 sheet By route: the same six rows and the same empty cells.
Proposed fix: Calculate the counts from the Interfaces sheet and keep the calculation rule on the sheet (done in v4: 20 In, 12 Out, 4 Both, 36 Total); the owner confirms the route vocabulary, which the Key sheet already defines, at the next review.

Title: Four services own no row of the disposition or the interface inventory
Detail: With the Service column filled, P3 rwb-case, S1 rwb-valuation, S2 rwb-treatment and S7 rwb-writeoff own no row of either sheet, although each has a contract of its own in Architecture v5. The reason is the shape of the source: it inventories the systems and the interfaces around recovery, and these four services consume those paths through P1 rwb-source-data and P2 rwb-integration instead of owning one. The inventory therefore reads as complete for the paths but not for the consumers, and a reader cannot see from it which service uses the write-off postings of INT-16 or the credit decision of INT-35.
Evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces row INT-16: 'GL / Write-off postings / In / File / ACE ingests the file / Monthly / DP13', owner ACE team; Architecture v5 slide 20 gives rwb-writeoff 'REST Source data: GL outcome'. v3 row INT-35 reads the NLEADS credit decision through v_ace_credit_decision; Architecture v5 slide 18 gives rwb-treatment the credit pack and the restructure calculator through rwb-integration. Slide 45: 'Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views ... Everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity'.
Proposed fix: Record the consumer of each path on the Service rules sheet when the Service Contract Catalog is next revised; no row is added here, because the inventory counts systems and interfaces and not consumers.

Title: No source names an owning service for any system or interface
Detail: The Service column that the realignment asks for has no source value. Version 3 gives an Owner of 'ACE team', 'Workbench' or 'Bank platform' on every row and names no service anywhere in the workbook; the Ownership Map v1 owns tables, endpoints, events and jobs and has no system or interface sheet. The owning service of each row is therefore derived from the scope of the 19 services in Architecture v5 and from ADR-010, and the derivation is written on the new Service rules sheet, one rule per path group (SR-01 to SR-19), so each filled cell can be traced to a slide, an ADR or an Ownership Map ruling.
Evidence: v3 sheet Disposition column E reads 'ACE team', 'Workbench' or 'Bank platform' on all 25 rows; v3 sheet Interfaces column J reads the same three values on all 36 rows. Ownership Map v1 sheets: Read me, Services, Tables, FK cuts, Endpoints (and the event, job and workflow sheets) - no system and no interface. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the data ownership per service.
Proposed fix: Confirm the 19 rules on the Service rules sheet with the architecture owner; where a rule changes, the Service cells of the rows it covers change with it.

Title: INT-33 (Legal Execution Department and courts) has no standard and two candidate services
Detail: INT-33 arrives 'Through partners', entered by the law firms in the partner portal, and its Standard and Decision cells read 'None'. The path spans two services: S4 rwb-litigation owns enforcement and court records, and S9 rwb-partner owns the partner instruction and the result the partner reports. The inventory records S4 as the owning service and keeps the partner entry on the Service rules sheet (SR-14). The standard stays 'None', because the contract of the partner gateway is specified in the partner portal design and not here.
Evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces: 'INT-33 / Legal Execution Department and courts / Enforcement and court records / In / Through partners / Through the law firms in the partner portal / As entered / DP07 / Not applicable / Workbench / E5 / None / None'. Architecture v5 slide 8: 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'; slide 19 gives rwb-litigation legal actions, hearings, judgments and enforcement and rwb-partner the instruction and the result.
Proposed fix: Decide whether INT-33 is a partner-result interface under S9 or an enforcement record under S4, and give it the standard of the partner gateway contract when the partner portal is built.

Title: Three statements of v3 read as outdated and are kept word for word
Detail: The Interfaces description says 'The Workbench owns its outbound files, the reporting feeds and the partner portal'; Architecture v5 has no reporting feed, and the partner portal sits behind the partner gateway in front of rwb-partner. The Disposition description says 'Supersedes v2', which was true of v3 and is not true of this version. The rest of the same sentences stays right: ACE ingests every inbound source, the Workbench owns the outbound files, and SMS, LINE and the audit logs leave through ACE paths. The rule of the run is to keep every value of the source and to change only what the realignment needs, so the three statements are unchanged and recorded here.
Evidence: v3 sheet Interfaces row 2: '36 numbered interfaces with 32 systems. ACE ingests every inbound source ... The Workbench owns its outbound files, the reporting feeds and the partner portal ...'. v3 sheet Disposition row 2: '25 systems and tools that recovery uses today, what happens to each, who owns the data path and when. Supersedes v2.' Architecture v5 slide 37 removes the data lake and Power BI feed; slide 8 replaces the external gateway with the partner gateway.
Proposed fix: Reword the two description rows at the next full revision of the inventory; the individual rows of the sheets give the owning service in the Service column meanwhile.

Title: The partner portal row keeps the wording of the external gateway
Detail: The disposition row for the partner portal says the screens run 'through the external gateway', and INT-24 gives the path 'Workbench screens through the external gateway' with OpenAPI 3.1. Architecture v5 slide 8 replaces the external gateway with the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) in the DMZ that fronts rwb-partner, and ADR-019 records the edge decision. The two cells are kept as written; the Service column names S9 rwb-partner, and the Service rules sheet records the gateway behind that choice.
Evidence: v3 sheet Disposition 'Partner portal': 'Does not exist / New / No / Workbench / Workbench screens for law firms, auction houses and buyers through the external gateway; needs the architecture change with one to three months of lead time / E5 / INT-24, INT-25 / DL03'. v3 sheet Interfaces INT-24: 'Both / Direct through ACE / Workbench screens through the external gateway / As entered / DP06, DP07, DP08'. Architecture v5 slide 8: 'Partners use the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner'.
Proposed fix: Reword both cells to the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) at the next full revision, and confirm the direction and the standard of INT-24 against the partner gateway contract.

Title: The source file is named v2 while its metadata table gives Version 1, and it carries no change-log row
Detail: The file is named v2 and dated 28 October 2026, while its metadata table gives Version 1 at the same date and the document has no change log. Version 3 is issued next to the file, the Supersedes row records the version the file name carries, and the change log records the source as row 1 because no row 2 exists.
Evidence: File name 'Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v2.docx'; metadata table rows '/ Version / 1 /' and '/ Date / 28 October 2026 /'; the document ends at section 7 Defects and contains no change-log table.
Proposed fix: Confirm whether the source carries version 1 or version 2, add the missing change-log row, and keep the file name and the metadata table in step from the next version on.

Title: The nine levels of version 2 describe one deployable and state no criteria for contract, component or wave integration testing
Detail: Version 2 has nine levels written for modules in one deployable with one schema and one API base: Integration means modules with a real PostgreSQL database and API contract means requests and responses against one OpenAPI file. The realignment needs a contract level for three contract shapes, a component level against fakes, and one integration test group per wave. The rows are added with who runs them, where and when, taken from Architecture v5 slides 11 and 46 and Template and Rules section R5.4; no source states their exit criteria, so the criteria written in the new rows are an assumption.
Evidence: Version 2 section 1: nine rows, Integration described as 'Modules with a real PostgreSQL database' and API contract as 'Requests and responses against the OpenAPI file'. Architecture v5 slide 11 gives five call types with one contract each (OpenAPI 3.1, AsyncAPI 3.0, contract jar, file manifest, SQL views); slide 46 states contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests and Testcontainers; Template and Rules R5.4 allows an I dependency on ITG stories only and R5.1 gives the integration epics RWB-ITG-W1 to RWB-ITG-W4.
Proposed fix: Confirm the exit criteria of the Contract, Component and integration-test-group levels and carry them into the Definition of Ready and Done, so that a story's Done and the level's exit agree.

Title: No source names the owner of a contract test or of a contract fake
Detail: The Ownership Map fixes the owner of every table, REST operation, event, workflow and job, but it names no test owner, and no source states who keeps a contract fake. Version 3 reads the test owner and the fake owner from the contract owner in the map: the service that publishes a contract owns its contract test and its fake.
Evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities, Jobs and Parameters give one owner code per item and hold no test column; version 2 section 5 names team types only: Developers, QA engineers, business testers, SCB IT security and role owners.
Proposed fix: Confirm that the owning service keeps the contract test and the fake of every contract it publishes, and state it in the Definition of Ready and Done and in the story template.

Title: How SIT is composed while a later-wave service does not exist is not stated
Detail: Services arrive in waves of 9, 4, 4 and 2, so in SIT during a wave some Recovery services do not exist yet. Version 3 states that the services of the wave under test run for real, that a fake never stands in for a service that exists in SIT, and that a later wave's published contract is served by its fake. No source states how SIT is composed across waves.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 38 gives the wave contents (Wave 1: nine services; Wave 2: P8, S2, S5, S8; Wave 3: S1, S3, S4, S6; Wave 4: S7, S9); Template and Rules R5.6 gives the wave map; version 2 section 2 names three environments and does not discuss a partly deployed Workbench.
Proposed fix: Confirm how SIT is composed for each wave: which services are deployed, which contracts are served by a fake, and how the fake is withdrawn when the owning service arrives.

Title: The environments are counted but never named in any source
Detail: Architecture v5 counts 19 x 4 environments and names none of them. Version 2 names DEV, SIT and UAT. Version 3 keeps the three environments the source names and does not name the fourth, which the count implies.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 45 answer: 'One cluster per service would be 19 x 4 environments'; slide 34 gives one Temporal cluster per environment and names no environment. Version 2 section 2: three rows, DEV, SIT and UAT.
Proposed fix: Publish the name, purpose and data rule of each of the four environments per service, so that every test level names the environment it runs in.

Title: Document control states Version 1 while the file is the second version

Evidence: Document control row 'Version / 1'; file name 'Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx'; the same table row 'Date / 28 October 2026'.

Title: User concurrency is written four ways across the sources
Detail: The load test is written for 410 simulated users. Non-functional specification v3 gives about 370 staff users (NFR-002) and about 50 partner users (NFR-003); Architecture v5 slide 48 notes 48 concurrent partner users and slide 33 notes about 420 concurrent users. Evidence: Load row '410 simulated users at three requests a minute for one hour'; NFR-002 'About 370 staff online in the busiest hour'; NFR-003 'About 50 partner users online'; Architecture v5 slide 33 note 'about 420 concurrent users (about 21 requests a second at peak)'; slide 48 note '320 partner users with 48 concurrent'.
Proposed fix: The 410 of the source is kept as the test load; the other readings are written next to it in section 2 with their source, so the mix can be set when the owner confirms the target.

Title: The release names E1 to E8 are not mapped to waves or epics

Evidence: When values 'Before E2 and E8', 'Before E2', 'Before E1 and E2', 'Before E1 and E5', 'Before E1', 'Each release'; Template and Rules R5.6 gives the wave map EP01 to EP08; Architecture v5 slide 38 gives waves 0 to 4 by epic.
Proposed fix: The eight names are kept as the source writes them and are read as the eight business epics EP01 to EP08; the wave order of section 9 is written from the Ownership Map wave of each service.

Title: Events that the event catalogue does not number cannot be named by an EV ID in a fake
Detail: The Ownership Map holds 30 numbered events (EV-01 to EV-30). Architecture v5 slide 43 adds further events without a number: RouteDecided, AssetSold, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged, FileDelivered and FileFailed. Proposed fix: Name each of those fakes by event name and topic in this plan; the number is added by the owner of the event catalogue and propagated to the fake when it exists.

Title: The daily journey smoke workflow has no data set in the plan
Detail: Architecture v5 slide 46 and slide 44 put a daily journey smoke workflow (JOB-22, PlatformSmokeWorkflow) in the platform, and it crosses the services in one journey. Version 3 lists the data for eleven tests but not for the smoke run.
Evidence: Architecture v5 slide 46: a daily journey smoke workflow (JOB-22). Ownership Map v1 sheet Jobs: JOB-22 Smoke workflow, owner PLT, 06:00. Version 3 section 3: eleven tests, none of them the smoke run.
Proposed fix: The smoke run uses the DEV seed of all 19 schemas and the fakes; it creates its own case per journey step and leaves the seed of the other tests untouched.

Title: The map gives six tables to the platform library but does not say which schema holds them
Detail: Sheet Tables assigns six tables to PLT: outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event, idempotency_key, feature_flag and feature_flag_change. PLT is not one of the 19 services and owns no schema, so the test data plan cannot seed them from a service row. Evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: six rows with owner PLT. Sheet Services: 19 services, none of them PLT. Architecture v5 slide 20: DB own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record.
Proposed fix: Create the four outbox, inbox and idempotency objects in all 19 schemas, as DP-09 requires, and keep feature_flag and feature_flag_change once, in rwb_integration, which serves the feature-flag admin API; the seed treats the four as per-schema tables.

Title: The metadata Version row reads 2 while the file family reads v3

Title: No contract version, compatibility or withdrawal rule is stated
Detail: Version 3 names no contract version, no compatibility rule and no way to withdraw a contract or a fake. Proposed fix: The v6 coverage block is kept unchanged as history and a realignment block is added below it.

Title: No issue-tracker, branch, commit or pull-request metadata
Detail: No issue, branch, commit or pull request exists for this run, and the run makes no external writes, so the matrix records none rather than an empty plausible value.
Evidence: R1 U6 (no issue-tracker access or updates); AGENTS.md rule 3 (no external writes, no commits)
Proposed fix: Add the metadata in the delivery tool when the work is scheduled; no value is invented here.

Title: Every realigned artifact is Draft with no approval
Detail: No human approval exists in this run, so every requirement, story, PRD and test artifact is Draft and the review status of each row is Draft.
Evidence: R1 U8 (no human verification stops in this run); the D-RCV-60 overlay assumes approval and continues.
Proposed fix: Run the verification loop before the first wave starts.

Title: Test cases of RWB-E2-023 have no story in the realignment plan
Detail: Test Cases v7 holds 9 cases for legacy story RWB-E2-023, all Parked. RWB-E2-023 appears in neither the split plan legacy table nor the legacy index, and Template and Rules R6 does not list it among the already-cancelled keys. Its disposition in the 19-service target is therefore unstated.
Evidence: 9 rows of Test Cases v7 with Story RWB-E2-023 and Status Parked; no entry in _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy and none in legacy_index.json.
Proposed fix: Record RWB-E2-023 as cancelled with the other Epic 1 cancels, or give it a story; its 9 cases stay parked meanwhile.

Title: Level vocabulary of Test Cases v7 is not the Template and Rules R7.2 vocabulary
Detail: Test Cases v7 states levels System, Access, Resilience, Operational and Schema (and Rule table in the rule sheet). Template and Rules R7.2 section 16 asks for Unit, Component, Contract, Integration, End to end and NFR. The two vocabularies have no stated mapping.
Evidence: Level column distinct values: System 1,234; Access 145; Resilience 58; Operational 19; Schema 1.
Proposed fix: Keep the source Level column unchanged and add a Test level column in the R7.2 vocabulary, with the mapping recorded as an assumption.

Title: Test Cases v7 covers 147 legacy keys of the 358 in the plan
Detail: Test Cases v7 holds cases for 147 legacy stories (Epic 1, Epic 2, Epic 3, Epic 4, Epic 8 and ACE). The plan holds 358 legacy keys and 1,034 stories. The other 211 legacy keys have no case in the workbook; their cases exist only in section 16 of their story files.
Evidence: 147 distinct Story values in the sheet; 358 keys in split_plan.json legacy; 1,416 test case identifiers in section 16 of the 147 integration stories alone.
Proposed fix: Read the case inventory from section 16 of each story file for the keys the workbook does not cover, in a later test-data step.

Title: A rule case names a route set, not the story or service that owns the rule set
Detail: The 448 rule cases name their route set (Restructure, Settlement, Deed in lieu, Guarantee claim, Litigation, Asset disposal, Debt sale, Write-off, Deviations, Universal rules) and no owning service, story or rule package. The plan carries no story for a rule package, so a rule case cannot be tied to a story key.
Evidence: Rule test cases sheet: 448 rows, Route set holds the ten names, no service column.
Proposed fix: Name the executing service of every route set from Architecture v5 slide 3 and leave the story key empty for a rule case.

Title: Neither workbook states the owner of a case
Detail: Test Cases v7 and Regression Suite v6 carry Story, Epic, Module and route set, and no owner column. The realignment assigns one owning service to every artefact, and the Template and Rules R7.2 section 16 expects a case to belong to a story of one service.
Evidence: No owner, service or team column in either workbook; 93 tables, 156 endpoints and 30 events carry an owner in the map.
Proposed fix: Add a Service column holding the owning service of the case from the Microservice Ownership Map v1.

Title: Two retired stories keep 20 live cases with no owning service
Detail: RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake) and RWB-TE-007 (Quartz scheduler) are retired under D-RCV-60 and get no new story, yet Test Cases v7 keeps 20 of their cases Live. Nothing states whether those cases are withdrawn or re-pointed at the replacement story.
Evidence: 9 rows for RWB-E1-014 and 11 rows for RWB-TE-007 with Status Live; Template and Rules R6 retires both.
Proposed fix: Mark the cases of the two retired stories as retired in the case sheet when the replacement stories are tested.

Title: Integration test case count of the Integration Test Plan is not held in Test Cases v7
Detail: Integration Test Plan v1 counts 1,416 test case identifiers in section 16 of the 147 integration stories, and Test Cases v7 holds no integration-level case at all. The two test documents therefore disagreed on the same cases.
Evidence: Integration Test Plan v1 sentence on 1,416 identifiers; Test Cases v7 Level column holds no Integration or End to end value.
Proposed fix: Add the -ITG case of every case the workbook already holds, as this version does, and let the plan count from the workbook.

Title: Regression Suite Growth sheet stops at release E6
Detail: The Growth sheet lists releases E1 to E6 and no wave 0 to 4 platform, integration or non-functional growth, while the target has 7 platform epics, 5 integration epics and 19 service stories in four waves. How the suite grows for the new platform and integration stories is therefore unstated.
Evidence: Growth sheet rows: Release E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6; no platform or integration row.
Proposed fix: Keep the Growth rows unchanged and state in the new Read me sheet that a new story's cases join the suite when its release ships.

Title: No environment or pipeline stage is stated for the platform cases
Detail: The 206 cases drafted from the 30 platform and integration stories that hold no legacy case need an environment and a stage. The test documents name DEV, SIT and UAT for the service cases and say nothing about where the platform baseline, Redis, DMZ gateway, schema and pipeline cases run.
Evidence: 206 drafted rows; Test Strategy v3 names DEV, SIT and UAT only for the service cases.
Proposed fix: State the environment and stage of the platform cases in the Test Data Plan, and keep the case rows environment-free until then.

Title: The v6 module column cannot show who builds a split row
Detail: A v6 row carries one monolith module (P1 to P10), one owner and one window. After the split, one v6 item is up to nine stories in up to six services, so neither the module column nor the By module counts can show the service or the lane that builds part of the item.
Evidence: v6 Sequence: 115 rows, 15 distinct module values, one row per item. Catalog: 530 stories carry the 115 legacy keys, across 19 services plus the platform and integration epics.
Proposed fix: Keep the module column for traceability and report load by service and lane, as the new sheet 'By service and lane' does.

Title: 124 non-CON stories carry no dependency row, 31 of them application stories
Detail: Of the 1,034 stories, 622 carry at least one dependency row. Of the 412 that carry none, 288 are CON stories, which correctly have no build dependency (Template and Rules R5.7 rule 1). The other 124 are non-CON: 57 DevOps, 31 App development, 18 Infrastructure, 11 ACE DB and 7 Integration. The OPS, INF and DB stories are the other team types' own work and the 7 ITG stories are harness stories. The 31 application stories take only the template-baseline contracts, so the catalog lists no row for them.
Evidence: Service Story Catalog v1: 1,034 stories, 622 with a row, 288 CON stories, 124 non-CON stories without a row (57 DevOps, 31 App development, 18 Infrastructure, 11 ACE DB, 7 Integration). All 939 Day 1 stories are in the catalog as Day 1.
Proposed fix: Publish the template baseline rule once on the Dependency classes sheet and keep the 31 application stories at Day 1; a story that turns out to have a real in-lane dependency gets the row in its own story file first, then in the next version of this map.

Title: Version 3 carries no change log and no tool line
Detail: Version 3 has no change log, so there is no record of what changed between version 2 and version 3 and no tool line for the source. Version 4 adds a change-log table, records version 3 as the source row with this gap and its assumption, and gives its own row the D-RCV-60 change and the tool line.
Evidence: The whole of version 3 was read: 18 paragraphs and 5 tables, with no change-log table, no version history and no tool line.
Proposed fix: Keep the change-log table in every later version and add the change log of versions 1 and 2 from the source history if it is ever found.

Title: No source states the board limit of a team type, or how many stories one team type may hold at once
Detail: Version 3 says that work in progress per squad stays within the board limit and gives no limit. The realignment replaces the two squads with five team types and 1034 stories, of which 939 are Day 1, so the board limit per team type decides how much of the Day-1 work can start at once and no source gives a number.
Evidence: Version 3 How to use it: 'Work in progress per squad stays within the board limit.' No number follows, and the document has no other capacity statement.
Proposed fix: Keep the board limit of version 3 unchanged until the programme states a limit per team type, then record it in this document and in the Day-1 Work Allocation.

Title: Version 3 names no release date for an item beyond the epic its window releases in
Detail: Version 3 states a window with a date range and a release line, 'releasing in Epic 1' to 'releasing in Epic 3', and no release date for an individual item. The story set of this run carries a release date per story, and the two do not line up one to one: the windows end on 22 January 2027 while the story set runs to 30 June 2027. This version keeps the release statement of version 3 and marks it tentative.
Evidence: Version 3 headings: 'Window 1, 2 to 13 November 2026' with '15 items, releasing in Epic 1'; the last heading 'Epic 3, 28 December 2026 to 22 January 2027' with '3 items, releasing in Epic 3'. No item carries a release date.
Proposed fix: State the release date of each window against the release calendar of the programme, kept tentative, and leave the epic statement as the item-level position until that calendar is agreed.

Title: The waits-on column of version 3 names legacy keys, and the stories that now carry those keys are different work items
Detail: Version 3 says 'Waits on names the items that must finish first, by their number within the same family' and lists keys such as E1-044 and TE-001. Those keys are not story keys in the realignment: each one is now a contract group and several stories, with a build dependency (H) that is allowed only inside a service or on a platform contract, a contract dependency (C) that never blocks, an integration dependency (I) that sits only on an integration story and external work (X) that is tracked only. No source translates a waits-on row of version 3 into the dependency classes of the realignment.
Evidence: Version 3 opening paragraph: 'Waits on names the items that must finish first, by their number within the same family'; Template and Rules R5.4 and R5.7 rules 2 to 8.
Proposed fix: Keep the waits-on column of version 3 word for word as the item-level position, and read the realigned waits of a story from its Ready to start and its lane.

Title: Issue tracker status of Epic 1 not readable in this run
Detail: Build status is taken from the realignment plan, not from the tracker (U6).
Proposed fix: Confirm in the verification loop

Title: Process 15.2 has no program requirement
Detail: L2 process 15.2 Test strategies (champion and challenger) is named only in the Epics 3 to 8 BRD scope for E8.
Evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1, section 7.1
